attributes.references: AWWA Process Control; ISA-88; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: ramp_rate_unit
attributes.description: The time unit denominator for the ramp_rate field (e.g., per_minute, per_hour). Clarifies the rate of change constraint for the setpoint transition.

attributes.name: scada_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI Historian or SCADA/PLC tag name that uniquely identifies the process variable associated with this setpoint (e.g., WTP01.CL2.RESIDUAL.SP, WTP01.FILTER1.TURBIDITY.HH). Used for real-time integration between the setpoint register and the SCADA/PI Historian system.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian Tag Naming Convention; ISA-5.1 Instrumentation Symbols and Identification

attributes.name: setpoint_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the setpoint parameter type within the facility's process control register (e.g., CL2_RESIDUAL_SP, PH_TARGET_SP, TURB_ALARM_HI). Used for cross-system integration and MOR regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: setpoint_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the process control setpoint parameter (e.g., 'Chlorine Residual Target', 'pH Target', 'Turbidity Alarm Threshold', 'Filter Run Time Limit', 'Chemical Dose Rate'). Serves as the primary identity label for the setpoint in operator interfaces and regulatory reports.
attributes.references: AWWA M56; EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (SWTR); OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: setpoint_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the setpoint record. 'active' indicates the setpoint is currently enforced in the control system. 'pending_approval' indicates it has been proposed but not yet approved by a certified operator. 'superseded' indicates it has been replaced by a newer version. 'under_review' indicates it is being evaluated for change.
attributes.references: AWWA Process Control; EPA SWTR Operator Certification; ISO 9001 Document Control

attributes.name: setpoint_value
attributes.description: The target or nominal value for the process control parameter. This is the principal quantitative fact — the value the control system actively maintains (e.g., 1.5 for chlorine residual in mg/L, 7.2 for pH, 0.1 for turbidity in NTU). Corresponds to the SP (setpoint) field in OSIsoft PI Historian.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian SP Attribute; AWWA M56; EPA SWTR CT Compliance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this setpoint was originated or last synchronized (e.g., OSIsoft_PI for PI Historian-sourced setpoints, SCADA_PLC for direct PLC configuration, Maximo for maintenance-driven setpoints, Manual_Entry for operator-entered values).
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; IBM Maximo Asset Management; SAP PM

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this setpoint record, incremented each time the setpoint value or limits are modified. Supports full version history and audit trail for regulatory compliance. Version 1 is the initial approved setpoint.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Document Control; AWWA Process Control; EPA SDWA

products.name: treatment_permit
products.description: Master record of operating permits governing treatment facility operations. Captures permit type (NPDES, state drinking water operating permit, air permit, residuals permit), permit number, issuing regulatory agency, issue date, expiration date, permitted flow limits (MGD), effluent/finished water quality limits, special conditions, renewal status, and associated facility. Authoritative permit register for the treatment domain supporting compliance management.
products.reference: NPDES / State Operating Permit Master

attributes.name: treatment_permit_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the treatment operating permit record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the treatment_permit data product.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Enterprise Data Model Convention

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the treatment facility (Water Treatment Plant or Wastewater Treatment Plant) to which this permit is issued. Links the permit to its regulated facility.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; SDWA Operating Permit Requirements

attributes.name: regulatory_agency_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory agency that issued this permit (e.g., EPA Region, State Primacy Agency, State Environmental Department). Used for compliance tracking and correspondence routing.
attributes.references: EPA; State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; NPDES Program

attributes.name: biosolids_permit_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit includes authorization for biosolids or residuals management (land application, incineration, or landfill disposal). Relevant for WWTPs subject to EPA 40 CFR Part 503 biosolids regulations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 (Biosolids Standards); CWA Section 405; WEF

attributes.name: bod_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Permitted maximum concentration of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) in treated effluent, expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). A primary indicator of organic pollution load in wastewater discharge. Used for DMR compliance evaluation.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards 40 CFR Part 133; CWA Section 301; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: chlorine_residual_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Minimum or maximum permitted chlorine residual concentration in finished water or treated effluent, expressed in mg/L. For drinking water, a minimum residual is required at the point of entry to the distribution system. For NPDES discharge, a maximum may be set to protect aquatic life.
attributes.references: SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.72 (Disinfection); EPA NPDES Aquatic Toxicity Limits; AWWA

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_end_date
attributes.description: The final date by which the facility must achieve full compliance with all permit limits per the regulatory-approved compliance schedule. Null if no compliance schedule is in effect. Used to track CIP project milestones and regulatory commitments.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.47; State Primacy Agency Compliance Schedule Requirements

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit includes a formal compliance schedule (a regulatory-approved timeline for achieving permit limits that the facility cannot currently meet). True triggers tracking of interim milestones and final compliance dates in the compliance management system.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.47 (Compliance Schedules); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: ct_requirement_mg_min_l
attributes.description: Minimum required CT (Contact Time) value for disinfection as specified in the permit, expressed in mg·min/L (product of disinfectant concentration and contact time). CT compliance is a core Surface Water Treatment Rule requirement for Giardia and virus inactivation credit.
attributes.references: EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (SWTR); LT2ESWTR; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.72; CT Guidance Manual

attributes.name: dmr_submission_method
attributes.description: The required or preferred method for submitting Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) or Monthly Operating Reports (MORs) to the regulatory agency. NetDMR is the EPA's electronic DMR system; eDMR refers to state-specific electronic systems; paper and state_portal are alternatives.
attributes.references: EPA NetDMR Program; 40 CFR Part 127 (NPDES Electronic Reporting Rule); State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: document_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference, file path, or URL pointing to the official permit document, fact sheet, and associated attachments stored in the enterprise document repository. Enables direct access to the authoritative permit text for compliance review.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Document Management Policy; AWWA Compliance Records Management

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit conditions become legally binding and enforceable. May differ from the issue date if a grace period or administrative continuance applies.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.21; State Primacy Agency Permit Conditions

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit term expires. Triggers renewal workflow and compliance calendar alerts. Under administrative continuance provisions, operations may continue under the expired permit while renewal is pending.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.6 (Administrative Continuance); SDWA; CWA Section 402

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Classification of the treatment facility covered by this permit. Water Treatment Plant (WTP) produces finished drinking water; Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) or Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) treats and discharges wastewater; pump_station may hold ancillary permits; combined covers co-located facilities.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; SDWA; AWWA; WEF

attributes.name: haa5_mcl_ug_l
attributes.description: Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for Haloacetic Acids (HAA5) as specified in the permit or applicable regulatory standard, expressed in micrograms per liter (µg/L). The EPA MCL for HAA5 is 60 µg/L. A key Disinfection Byproduct (DBP) compliance parameter for drinking water permits.
attributes.references: EPA Stage 2 DBPR; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.64; HAA5 MCL

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory agency formally issued or reissued the permit. Marks the start of the current permit term and is used to calculate permit age and renewal lead times.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Administration; SDWA; CWA

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory compliance inspection conducted by the issuing agency or primacy agency at the permitted facility. Used to track inspection frequency, prepare for upcoming inspections, and assess compliance standing.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Compliance Inspection Program; SDWA Sanitary Survey Requirements; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency of effluent or finished water quality monitoring as specified in the permit. Drives the sampling schedule in the LIMS and the reporting calendar for DMR/MOR submissions. Represents the most frequent monitoring requirement across all parameters.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Monitoring Requirements; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; State Primacy Agency Monitoring Plans

attributes.name: next_inspection_date
attributes.description: Anticipated or scheduled date of the next regulatory compliance inspection. Supports proactive compliance preparation and internal audit scheduling. May be estimated based on inspection frequency requirements.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Compliance Inspection Program; SDWA Sanitary Survey Schedule; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, regulatory correspondence summaries, internal compliance observations, or context not captured in structured fields. Used by compliance staff to document permit history, agency communications, and action items.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Compliance Management Policy; AWWA Compliance Records Management

attributes.name: npdes_major_minor_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Major/Minor Classification
attributes.description: EPA classification of the NPDES permit as major or minor based on facility size, discharge volume, and potential environmental impact. Major facilities are subject to more stringent oversight, mandatory DMR reporting, and EPA inspection priorities. Applicable only to NPDES permit types.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; 40 CFR Part 122; EPA ICIS-NPDES Classification Criteria

attributes.name: permit_category
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit is an individual permit (facility-specific terms and conditions), a general permit (covers a category of similar dischargers), or an emergency permit (temporary authorization). Determines the regulatory review process and compliance obligations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.28 (General Permits); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: permit_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name or title of the permit as assigned by the issuing agency or used internally (e.g., 'City Water Treatment Plant NPDES Discharge Permit', 'Regional WTP Drinking Water Operating Permit'). Supports human-readable identification in compliance registers and reports.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Permit Register; AWWA Compliance Management Best Practices

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Externally-assigned permit number as issued by the regulatory authority (e.g., NPDES permit number, state drinking water operating permit number). This is the official identifier used in all regulatory correspondence, DMRs, MORs, and CCRs.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; SDWA; CWA; State Primacy Agency Permit Numbering

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the permit. Active indicates the permit is in force; pending_renewal indicates the renewal application has been submitted and the permit is administratively continued; expired indicates the permit term has lapsed without renewal; suspended or revoked indicates regulatory action has been taken.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Administration; SDWA Operating Permit Lifecycle; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the permit by regulatory program. NPDES governs wastewater discharge under the Clean Water Act; drinking_water_operating governs WTP operations under SDWA; air_emission covers process air releases; residuals_management covers biosolids/sludge disposal; industrial_pretreatment covers IUP programs; stormwater covers MS4 or industrial stormwater. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NPDES|drinking_water_operating|air_emission|residuals_management|industrial_pretreatment|stormwater|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CWA Section 402 (NPDES); SDWA; EPA 40 CFR Parts 122-125; State Primacy Agency Regulations

attributes.name: permitted_avg_flow_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Permitted Average Flow (Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Monthly average flow rate authorized under this permit in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). Distinct from the peak daily limit; used for long-term capacity planning and average-basis compliance evaluation in DMR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Effluent Limitations Guidelines; 40 CFR Part 122 Appendix A

attributes.name: permitted_flow_mgd
attributes.description: Maximum daily flow rate authorized under this permit, expressed in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). This is the principal quantitative limit governing facility capacity and is used for capacity planning, compliance monitoring, and MOR/DMR reporting.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Effluent Limitations; SDWA Maximum Contaminant Levels; AWWA M1 Manual

attributes.name: pfas_monitoring_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Monitoring Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit requires monitoring for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) compounds. Reflects EPA's PFAS Action Plan and emerging state-level PFAS MCLs. Drives LIMS sampling plan configuration and CCR disclosure requirements.
attributes.references: EPA PFAS Action Plan; SDWA PFAS MCL Rule (2024); State PFAS Monitoring Requirements; AWWA

attributes.name: ph_limit_max
attributes.description: Maximum permitted pH value for treated effluent or finished water as specified in the permit. Used alongside ph_limit_min to define the acceptable pH range for compliance monitoring and corrosion control program evaluation.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.21; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: ph_limit_min
attributes.description: Minimum permitted pH value for treated effluent or finished water as specified in the permit. pH is a key indicator of water chemistry and corrosion control. Typically 6.0–9.0 for NPDES effluent; 6.5–8.5 for drinking water under SDWA.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.21; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: receiving_water_body
attributes.description: Name of the surface water body (river, lake, estuary, or ocean) designated as the receiving water for permitted discharges (e.g., 'Ohio River', 'Lake Michigan'). Required for NPDES permits; used in water quality impact assessments and antidegradation analysis.
attributes.references: CWA Section 303; EPA NPDES Permit Application; 40 CFR Part 131 (Water Quality Standards)

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit renewal application was submitted to the issuing regulatory agency. NPDES regulations typically require submission at least 180 days before expiration. Used to verify timely renewal and administrative continuance eligibility.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.21(d); State Primacy Agency Renewal Requirements

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the permit renewal process. Tracks progression from initial application through agency review to final determination. Supports compliance calendar management and regulatory relationship tracking.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Renewal Process; SDWA Operating Permit Renewal; AWWA Compliance Management

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for submitting compliance reports (DMRs, MORs, or equivalent) to the regulatory agency as specified in the permit. Drives the compliance reporting calendar and submission deadlines tracked in the MOR submission workflow.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES DMR Reporting Requirements; SDWA MOR Requirements; 40 CFR Part 122.41(l)

attributes.name: special_conditions
attributes.description: Narrative description of any special conditions, schedules of compliance, best management practices (BMPs), or additional requirements imposed by the regulatory agency beyond standard effluent limitations. Examples include PFAS monitoring requirements, CSO long-term control plan milestones, or LCRR service line inventory obligations.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Special Conditions; SDWA; LCRR; PFAS Action Plan; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: term_years
attributes.description: Duration of the permit in years as specified by the issuing agency. NPDES permits are typically issued for 5-year terms; state drinking water operating permits may vary. Used for renewal planning and compliance scheduling.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.46 (NPDES 5-year term); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: tss_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Permitted maximum concentration of Total Suspended Solids (TSS) in treated effluent, expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). Core secondary treatment standard for WWTP NPDES compliance. Used in DMR reporting and effluent quality monitoring.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards 40 CFR Part 133; CWA Section 301; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: tthm_mcl_ug_l
attributes.description: Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for Total Trihalomethanes (TTHMs) as specified in the permit or applicable regulatory standard, expressed in micrograms per liter (µg/L). The EPA MCL for TTHMs is 80 µg/L. A key Disinfection Byproduct (DBP) compliance parameter for drinking water permits.
attributes.references: EPA Stage 2 Disinfectants and Disinfection Byproducts Rule (Stage 2 DBPR); SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.64; MCL

attributes.name: turbidity_limit_ntu
attributes.description: Maximum permitted turbidity of finished water or treated effluent in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). For WTPs, the Surface Water Treatment Rule requires combined filter effluent turbidity not to exceed 0.3 NTU in 95% of measurements. Critical for MCL compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (SWTR); LT2ESWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.73; SDWA MCL

attributes.name: violation_count_active
attributes.description: Number of currently unresolved permit violations (effluent limit exceedances, reporting violations, or schedule of compliance violations) associated with this permit. Sourced from the regulatory agency's compliance tracking system. Used for compliance risk scoring and executive reporting.
attributes.references: EPA ECHO (Enforcement and Compliance History Online); NPDES Compliance Tracking; State Agency

products.name: treatment_violation
products.description: Records treatment-related regulatory violations and exceedances at WTP/WWTP facilities. Captures violation type (MCL exceedance, treatment technique violation, monitoring and reporting violation, CT violation, turbidity violation), violation date, contaminant or parameter, measured value, regulatory limit, severity level, public notification requirement triggered, corrective action plan, resolution date, and regulatory agency notification status. Supports compliance management and public notification workflows.
products.reference: SDWA / NPDES Regulatory Violation Record

attributes.name: treatment_violation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each treatment regulatory violation record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: chemical_dose_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.chemical_dose_event. Business justification: Treatment violations (e.g., MCL exceedances, CT failures) are often caused by or directly linked to a specific chemical dosing event — under-dosing of disinfectant, incorrect chemical concentration, o

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.cip_project. Business justification: Regulatory violations (MCL exceedances, CT failures) frequently trigger CIP projects for infrastructure upgrades. Utilities must demonstrate to regulators that a capital project was initiated in respo

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) or Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) facility where the violation occurred.

attributes.name: filter_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.filter_run. Business justification: Turbidity MCL exceedances and filter performance violations are directly tied to specific filter runs. treatment_violation has process_area (STRING) but no FK to the specific filter_run that caused th

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Violations trigger penalty costs (penalty_amount field present), corrective action expenses, and legal fees. Required for penalty accrual, corrective action cost tracking, regulatory cost reporting, a

attributes.name: primary_treatment_analytical_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.analytical_result. Business justification: Treatment violations are triggered by specific analytical results exceeding regulatory limits. Linking treatment_violation directly to the triggering analytical_result provides the evidentiary basis f

attributes.name: process_reading_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.process_alarm. Business justification: Treatment violations are often triggered by process alarms (e.g., CT compliance failure, turbidity exceedance). The scada_alarm_tag string on treatment_violation should be replaced by FK to the treatm

attributes.name: process_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.process_unit. Business justification: treatment_violation has process_area as a free-text STRING field identifying where the violation occurred. Normalizing this to process_unit_id provides a structured FK to the specific treatment proces

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Treatment violations are tied to specific assets (failed filter, malfunctioning UV reactor). Linking violations to the asset registry enables asset-level violation history for criticality rating updat

attributes.name: regulatory_agency_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory agency (e.g., EPA, State Primacy Agency) to which this violation must be reported.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: source_water_intake_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.source_water_intake. Business justification: Treatment violations can be triggered by source water quality events — high turbidity, algal blooms, or contamination events at the intake. source_water_intake captures these raw water quality paramet

attributes.name: territory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.territory. Business justification: SDWA Tier 1/2/3 public notification requirements mandate identifying the affected service territory when treatment violations occur. treatment_violation already has public_notification_required and pu

attributes.name: treatment_permit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit ID
attributes.description: Reference to the NPDES permit under which the violation was recorded, applicable for wastewater discharge violations at WWTP facilities.
attributes.references: EPA CWA Section 402; NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IBM Maximo CMMS work order created to execute the corrective action plan for this violation. Links compliance management to maintenance and operations workflows.

attributes.name: ccr_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation must be disclosed in the annual Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) sent to customers, as required by EPA SDWA regulations for community water systems.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart O; Consumer Confidence Report Rule

attributes.name: contaminant_code
attributes.description: EPA or state-assigned contaminant code for the parameter that was violated (e.g., TTHM for Total Trihalomethanes, PFAS, turbidity, lead, copper, BOD, TSS). Aligns with EPA SDWIS contaminant codes.
attributes.references: EPA SDWIS Contaminant Code List; EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141

attributes.name: contaminant_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the contaminant or treatment parameter involved in the violation (e.g., Total Trihalomethanes, Turbidity, Lead, Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)).

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which the corrective action plan must be completed and compliance restored, as agreed with the regulatory agency or mandated by the compliance schedule.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Compliance Schedules; AWWA

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan
attributes.description: Narrative description of the corrective action plan developed to address the root cause of the violation and restore compliance. Includes immediate remediation steps, process adjustments, and preventive measures.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA Compliance Management; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this violation record was first created in the compliance management system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the violation was detected, either through SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian alarm, laboratory result, or operator observation. Supports CT compliance and public notification deadline calculations.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.85; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: dmr_reporting_period
attributes.description: The DMR reporting period (YYYY-MM) in which this violation must be included for NPDES permit compliance reporting. Applicable for WWTP effluent violations. Links to the corresponding DMR submission.

attributes.name: enforcement_action_taken
attributes.description: Indicates whether the regulatory agency has initiated a formal enforcement action (e.g., Notice of Violation, Administrative Order, Consent Order, penalty) in response to this violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA Enforcement and Compliance Assurance; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: enforcement_action_type
attributes.description: Type of formal enforcement action taken by the regulatory agency (e.g., Notice of Violation (NOV), Administrative Order (AO), Consent Order, Civil Penalty, Criminal Referral). Null if no enforcement action was taken. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NOV|administrative_order|consent_order|civil_penalty|criminal_referral|compliance_schedule|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA Enforcement and Compliance Assurance; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: exceedance_magnitude
attributes.description: The numeric difference between the measured value and the regulatory limit (measured_value minus regulatory_limit). Positive values indicate the degree of exceedance above the limit, supporting severity assessment and trend analysis.

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Type of treatment facility where the violation occurred: WTP (Water Treatment Plant), WWTP (Wastewater Treatment Plant), STP (Sewage Treatment Plant), booster station, or storage facility.

attributes.name: is_repeat_violation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation is a repeat occurrence of the same contaminant or parameter violation at the same facility within the preceding 12-month period. Repeat violations may trigger escalated regulatory response and increased penalties.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs; AWWA Compliance Analytics

attributes.name: measured_value
attributes.description: The actual measured concentration, level, or parameter value recorded at the time of the violation (e.g., turbidity in NTU, chlorine residual in mg/L, BOD in mg/L, CT value in mg·min/L). This is the quantitative result that triggered the violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; LIMS (LabWare)

attributes.name: measured_value_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the measured_value field (e.g., mg/L for chemical concentrations, NTU for Nephelometric Turbidity Units, mg·min/L for CT Contact Time, CFU/100mL for microbial counts). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|NTU|mg·min/L|CFU/100mL|pH|mg/kg|ug/L|pCi/L|MPN/100mL — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; AWWA; ISO 9001

attributes.name: mor_reporting_period
attributes.description: The MOR reporting period (YYYY-MM) in which this violation must be included for regulatory submission. Links the violation to the corresponding Monthly Operating Report for the facility.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency MOR Requirements; AWWA

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the certified treatment plant operator to record observations, circumstances, and contextual information about the violation at the time of detection or during investigation.
attributes.references: AWWA; State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monetary penalty assessed by the regulatory agency for this violation, in USD. Supports financial liability tracking, OPEX reporting, and GAAP/GASB financial disclosures for municipal utilities.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; GAAP; GASB; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: The operating permit number (e.g., NPDES permit number, state drinking water permit) under which the facility operates and against which the violation is recorded. Used in regulatory correspondence and DMR/MOR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES; EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: public_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which public notification was issued to customers and the public in accordance with the EPA Public Notification Rule. Null if notification has not yet been issued.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Oracle Utilities CC&B

attributes.name: public_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation triggers a mandatory public notification requirement under EPA SDWA Public Notification Rule (40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q). True when the violation type and severity mandate customer and public notification.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Public Notification Rule

attributes.name: public_notification_tier
attributes.description: EPA Public Notification Rule tier classification: Tier 1 requires notification within 24 hours (acute health risk); Tier 2 requires notification within 30 days; Tier 3 requires annual notification. Drives notification workflow and deadline management.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Public Notification Rule

attributes.name: regulatory_limit
attributes.description: The applicable Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL), treatment technique standard, or permit limit that was exceeded or violated. For CT violations, this is the required CT value in mg·min/L.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; AWWA; LCRR

attributes.name: regulatory_limit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory standard that was violated: MCL (Maximum Contaminant Level), MCLG (Maximum Contaminant Level Goal), treatment technique standard, NPDES permit limit, action level (e.g., Lead and Copper Rule), or required CT (Contact Time for Disinfection).
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; LCRR; AWWA

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory agency (EPA or State Primacy Agency) was formally notified of this violation, as required by SDWA or NPDES permit conditions.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA NPDES; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_status
attributes.description: Status of the formal notification to the regulatory agency (EPA or State Primacy Agency) regarding this violation. Tracks whether notification is pending, has been submitted, has been acknowledged, or is overdue per regulatory deadlines.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs; NACWA

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the violation was resolved and compliance was restored, confirmed by a return-to-compliance sample result or regulatory acknowledgment. Null if the violation remains open.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the root cause of the violation to support trend analysis and preventive action programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|process_upset|operator_error|source_water_event|chemical_dosing|monitoring_failure|reporting_failure|infrastructure|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA; WEF; ISO 14001 Environmental Management; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Assessed severity classification of the violation based on the degree of exceedance, public health risk, and regulatory consequence. Critical indicates immediate public health risk; high indicates significant exceedance; medium indicates moderate concern; low indicates minor or administrative violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA Compliance Management Best Practices; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this violation record was last modified in the compliance management system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and incremental Silver Layer processing.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB

attributes.name: violation_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the treatment violation or regulatory exceedance was first identified or occurred, as recorded in the compliance management system.

attributes.name: violation_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to this violation record, used in regulatory correspondence, public notifications, and compliance tracking systems.
attributes.references: EPA Safe Drinking Water Information System (SDWIS); AWWA

attributes.name: violation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the violation record, tracking its progression from identification through corrective action to regulatory closure.
attributes.references: EPA SDWIS; AWWA Compliance Management Best Practices

attributes.name: violation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory violation category. MCL exceedance indicates a Maximum Contaminant Level was exceeded; treatment technique indicates a required process was not followed; monitoring and reporting indicates a missed sample or late report; CT violation indicates Contact Time for disinfection was insufficient; turbidity violation indicates NTU limits were breached. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mcl_exceedance|treatment_technique|monitoring_reporting|ct_violation|turbidity_violation|public_notification|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; AWWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

domains.name: customer

products.name: customer_account

This is the primary anchor entity for the customer domain — all billing, metering, service delivery, and regulatory reporting references flow through this entity.

products.name: person

Captures pipe material (ductile iron, PVC, HDPE, cast iron), nominal diameter, installation year, pressure class, lining type, coating type, operating pressure zone, DMA assignment, GIS geometry (from Esri ArcGIS), Innovyze InfoWater model node references, condition grade, and lifecycle status. SSOT for distribution pipe inventory.

attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Pipe mains are physical infrastructure assets requiring lifecycle tracking, depreciation, and capital renewal planning in the asset registry. Every water utility registers pipe mains as fixed assets.

attributes.name: asset_owner
attributes.description: Legal owner of the pipe main asset. Typically the water utility, but may be a municipality, private developer, or other entity. Important for maintenance responsibility and capital planning.

attributes.name: average_daily_flow_gpm
attributes.description: Average daily flow through the pipe main in gallons per minute (GPM), typically derived from SCADA flow meters or hydraulic model calibration. Used for demand analysis and capacity utilization assessment.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: bedding_type
attributes.description: Type of bedding material and installation method used to support the pipe main in the trench. Common types include sand, gravel, crushed stone, and controlled low-strength material (CLSM). Affects pipe structural integrity and longevity.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: break_history_count
attributes.description: Total number of main breaks or failures recorded for this pipe main since installation. High break counts indicate poor condition and prioritize replacement. Used for reliability analysis and risk assessment.
attributes.references: AWWA M28 Rehabilitation of Water Mains

attributes.name: cathodic_protection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the pipe main is protected by a cathodic protection system to prevent corrosion. True if cathodic protection is installed and active; false otherwise. Primarily applicable to metallic pipes (ductile iron, steel).

attributes.name: coating_type
attributes.description: Exterior coating material applied to the pipe main to protect against soil corrosion and environmental degradation. Common coatings include polyethylene wrap, epoxy, and zinc.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pipe main record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: depth_feet
attributes.description: Depth of the pipe main below ground surface in feet, measured to the pipe crown. Affects frost protection, traffic load resistance, and excavation cost for repairs.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: downstream_node_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the downstream hydraulic node (junction, tank, reservoir, or pump) in the distribution network topology. Used for hydraulic modeling in Innovyze InfoWater and network connectivity analysis.

attributes.name: fire_flow_capable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the pipe main is sized and pressurized to provide adequate fire flow per AWWA and Insurance Services Office (ISO) standards. True if the main meets fire flow requirements; false otherwise.
attributes.references: AWWA M31 Distribution System Requirements for Fire Protection

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the pipe main feature in the Esri ArcGIS spatial database. Links the asset record to its geographic representation for mapping, spatial analysis, and field operations.

attributes.name: gis_geometry_wkt

attributes.description: Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the pipe main centerline geometry (LINESTRING). Captures the spatial path of the pipe for GIS integration, routing, and proximity analysis.

attributes.name: hazen_williams_c_factor
attributes.description: Hazen-Williams roughness coefficient (C-factor) used in hydraulic modeling to represent pipe friction and head loss. New pipes typically have C=130-140; older or corroded pipes may have C=80-100. Used in Innovyze InfoWater hydraulic models.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation, Innovyze InfoWater

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the pipe main was installed and placed into service. Used for age-based condition assessment, remaining useful life calculations, and capital improvement planning (CIP).

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the pipe main was installed. Commonly used for age-based analysis and replacement prioritization when exact installation date is unknown.

attributes.name: joint_type
attributes.description: Type of joint used to connect pipe segments. Common types include push-on, mechanical joint, flanged, welded, and restrained joint. Joint type affects installation cost, seismic resilience, and leak risk.

attributes.name: last_break_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent main break or failure event on this pipe main. Used for failure trend analysis and to assess time since last incident.
attributes.references: AWWA M28 Rehabilitation of Water Mains

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical inspection of the pipe main. Used to track inspection compliance and schedule future inspections per preventive maintenance (PM) schedules.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pipe main record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: length_feet
attributes.description: Physical length of the pipe main segment in feet, measured from upstream to downstream node. Used for network inventory, hydraulic modeling, and asset valuation.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the pipe main in its asset lifecycle. Active pipes are in service; planned pipes are in design or budgeted; abandoned pipes are no longer used but not removed.

attributes.name: lining_type
attributes.description: Interior lining material applied to the pipe main to prevent corrosion and maintain water quality. Common linings include cement mortar, epoxy, polyurethane, and polyethylene. Critical for compliance with Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR).

attributes.name: maintenance_responsibility
attributes.description: Entity responsible for operations and maintenance (O&M) of the pipe main. May differ from asset owner in cases of shared infrastructure or developer-owned systems pending transfer.

attributes.name: material
attributes.description: Material composition of the pipe main. Common materials include ductile iron (DI), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), cast iron (CI), and steel. Material affects durability, corrosion resistance, and hydraulic performance. attributes.references: AWWA C151 Ductile-Iron Pipe, AWWA C900 PVC Pipe

attributes.name: max_flow_capacity_gpm
attributes.description: Maximum hydraulic flow capacity of the pipe main in gallons per minute (GPM) under design conditions. Calculated based on diameter, pressure, and Hazen-Williams C-factor. Used for capacity planning and fire flow analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: nominal_diameter_inches
attributes.description: Nominal inside diameter of the pipe main in inches. Standard sizes range from 2 inches for service lines to 72+ inches for transmission mains. Critical for hydraulic capacity and flow (GPM/MGD) calculations.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to the pipe main. May include historical information, operational constraints, or field observations.

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Typical operating pressure in pounds per square inch (PSI) at which the pipe main operates under normal conditions. Used for hydraulic analysis and to ensure adequate service pressure (typically 40-80 PSI at customer meters).
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: pipe_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the pipe main, typically assigned by the utility for asset tracking and field reference. May follow utility-specific numbering conventions.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: pipe_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pipe main by its function in the water distribution system. Transmission mains convey large volumes between facilities; distribution mains serve neighborhoods; service laterals connect to premises.
attributes.references: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe Design and Installation

attributes.name: pressure_class_psi
attributes.description: Rated working pressure class of the pipe main in pounds per square inch (PSI). Common classes include 150, 200, 250, 300 PSI. Must meet or exceed the operating pressure of the assigned pressure zone.

attributes.name: street_name
attributes.description: Name of the street or roadway where the pipe main is located. Used for field crew dispatch, work order management, and public communication during maintenance or repairs.

attributes.name: warranty_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the manufacturer or contractor warranty for the pipe main expires. Used for warranty claim management and defect tracking.

products.name: service_line
products.description: Master record for individual customer service connections from the distribution main to the meter setter, including material (lead, galvanized, copper, HDPE), diameter, installation year, length, LCRR material classification (lead, non-lead, unknown), GIS coordinates, pressure zone, and connection status. Critical for Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) compliance inventory. Links to meter and customer account in respective domains.
products.reference: EPA LCRR Service Line Inventory; AWWA M58

attributes.name: service_line_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the individual customer service connection from the distribution main to the meter setter. Primary key for service line records.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.cip_project. Business justification: Lead service line replacement programs (LCRR compliance) are tracked as CIP projects. Each service line replacement requires project attribution for cost tracking, grant reimbursement, regulatory repo

attributes.name: compliance_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_permit. Business justification: Service connections operate under utility permits. LCRR compliance requires linking service lines to permit conditions for lead/copper monitoring, material inventory reporting, and replacement program

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer billing account served by this service line. Links service infrastructure to customer billing domain.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing (CC&B)

attributes.name: dma_id

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Service lines are capitalized infrastructure requiring depreciation and asset valuation, especially critical for LCRR lead replacement cost tracking and capital improvement planning in rate cases.

attributes.name: installation_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Service line installation/replacement contractors tracked for LCRR program contractor management, installation quality assurance, performance tracking, and warranty management in lead service line rep

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Service lines are procured materials (copper, lead, plastic). Critical for LCRR compliance requiring material specification tracking and procurement records for lead service line inventory and replace

attributes.name: metering_meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the water meter installed at the terminus of this service line for consumption measurement.

attributes.name: pipe_main_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.pipe_main. Business justification: Each service line originates from a distribution main; linking to pipe_main provides a parent relationship and eliminates the need for storing pipe_main details redundantly.

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical premise or property location served by this service line.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing (CC&B)

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.pressure_zone. Business justification: service_line currently stores pressure_zone_code as a denormalized STRING attribute. Normalizing this to a proper FK pressure_zone_id → pressure_zone.pressure_zone_id eliminates data redundancy and en

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: Service lines are capital assets requiring LCRR compliance tracking, depreciation schedules, and replacement cost accounting. Essential for regulatory inventory reporting and financial asset valuation

attributes.name: replacement_grant_id

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality where the service line is located.

attributes.name: connection_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the service line connection indicating whether it is actively serving a customer or has been deactivated.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service line record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: curb_stop_installed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a curb stop shutoff valve is installed on the service line for isolation purposes.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: curb_stop_location
attributes.description: Descriptive location of the curb stop valve for field crew reference during service shutoff operations.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: diameter_inches
attributes.description: Internal diameter of the service line pipe measured in inches. Typical residential service lines range from 0.75 to 2.0 inches.
attributes.references: AWWA M22 Sizing Water Service Lines and Meters

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier in the Esri ArcGIS system linking this service line record to the corresponding GIS spatial feature.

attributes.name: gis_latitude
attributes.description: Latitude coordinate of the service line connection point in decimal degrees for GIS mapping and spatial analysis.

attributes.name: gis_longitude
attributes.description: Longitude coordinate of the service line connection point in decimal degrees for GIS mapping and spatial analysis.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the service line was originally installed and connected to the distribution main.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year of service line installation. Used for age-based risk assessment and replacement prioritization when exact installation date is unknown.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical inspection or condition assessment of the service line.

attributes.name: last_leak_repair_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent leak repair performed on this service line.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service line record was most recently updated.

attributes.name: lcrr_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) Material Classification
attributes.description: EPA LCRR regulatory classification of service line material status for lead service line inventory and replacement planning. Mandatory for LCRR compliance reporting.
