attributes.name: lcrr_inventory_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) Inventory Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the service line material classification has been physically verified for LCRR compliance inventory accuracy.
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) 2021

attributes.name: lcrr_verification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) Verification Date
attributes.description: Date when the service line material was physically verified for LCRR inventory compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) 2021

attributes.name: lcrr_verification_method
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) Verification Method
attributes.description: Method used to verify the service line material classification for LCRR compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) 2021

attributes.name: leak_history_count
attributes.description: Total number of documented leak incidents on this service line since installation. Used for reliability assessment and replacement prioritization.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: length_feet
attributes.description: Total measured length of the service line from the distribution main tap to the meter setter, measured in feet.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: material_type
attributes.description: Material composition of the service line pipe. Critical for Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) compliance and corrosion risk assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: lead|galvanized_steel|copper|polyethylene|pvc|hdpe|unknown — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) 2021

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special conditions, or historical information about the service line.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Designation of ownership responsibility for the service line. Determines maintenance and replacement liability between utility and property owner.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the service line location.

attributes.name: replacement_method
attributes.description: Planned or executed method for service line replacement. Trenchless methods minimize surface disruption.
attributes.references: AWWA M28 Rehabilitation of Water Mains

attributes.name: replacement_priority_score
attributes.description: Calculated priority score for service line replacement based on age, material, leak history, and LCRR compliance requirements. Higher scores indicate higher replacement urgency.
attributes.references: AWWA M28 Rehabilitation of Water Mains

attributes.name: service_line_number
attributes.description: Business identifier or tag number assigned to the service connection for field operations and customer reference.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service line based on customer type and usage category.
attributes.references: AWWA M22 Sizing Water Service Lines and Meters

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province where the service line is located.

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Street address of the property served by this service line for field operations and customer correspondence.

attributes.name: tap_size_inches
attributes.description: Diameter of the tap connection point on the distribution main where the service line originates, measured in inches.
attributes.references: AWWA M22 Sizing Water Service Lines and Meters

products.name: pressure_zone
products.description: Master record defining hydraulic pressure zones within the distribution network. Captures zone name, target operating pressure range (PSI min/max), design pressure, elevation range, boundary description, associated storage facilities, PRV stations controlling the zone, and Innovyze InfoWater hydraulic model zone reference. Used for pressure management, NRW analysis, and DMA boundary definition.
products.reference: Innovyze InfoWater pressure zone; AWWA M32 Distribution Network Analysis

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the pressure zone within the distribution network. Primary key.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: compliance_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_permit. Business justification: Pressure zones are operational units subject to permit conditions for minimum pressure requirements, water quality monitoring locations, and disinfection residual compliance. Permit conditions specify

attributes.name: primary_storage_facility_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary storage tank or reservoir that serves this pressure zone, providing hydraulic head and emergency storage.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: revenue_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_requirement. Business justification: Cost-of-service studies and rate design allocate revenue requirements by pressure zone or service area. Water utility rate cases require zone-level O&M and capital cost allocation. Finance and regulat

attributes.name: arcgis_feature_code
attributes.description: Corresponding feature identifier in the Esri ArcGIS Geographic Information System (GIS) for spatial representation and network topology management.

attributes.name: average_daily_demand_mgd
attributes.description: Average daily water demand in Million Gallons per Day (MGD) for the pressure zone, used for capacity planning and hydraulic modeling.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: average_elevation_ft
attributes.description: Average ground elevation in feet above sea level across the pressure zone, used for hydraulic modeling and demand allocation.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: boundary_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the geographic or infrastructure boundaries defining the pressure zone, including major streets, landmarks, or infrastructure features.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the pressure zone was officially commissioned and placed into active service for water distribution operations.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pressure zone record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: Total number of active customer service connections within the pressure zone, used for demand forecasting and revenue allocation.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: design_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Design or nominal operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) for which the zone infrastructure was engineered and constructed.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: elevation_max_ft
attributes.description: Maximum ground elevation in feet above sea level within the pressure zone boundary, critical for pressure management and PRV settings.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: elevation_min_ft
attributes.description: Minimum ground elevation in feet above sea level within the pressure zone boundary, used for hydraulic gradient calculations.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: fire_flow_capacity_gpm
attributes.description: Minimum fire flow capacity in Gallons per Minute (GPM) that the pressure zone must maintain at specified residual pressure for fire protection, per Insurance Services Office (ISO) and NFPA standards.
attributes.references: NFPA 1142 - Standard on Water Supplies for Suburban and Rural Fire Fighting; ISO Fire Suppression Rating Schedule

attributes.name: hydraulic_model_last_calibrated_date
attributes.description: Date when the hydraulic model for this pressure zone was last calibrated against field measurements, ensuring model accuracy for planning and operational decisions.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: infowater_model_zone_code
attributes.description: Corresponding pressure zone identifier in the Innovyze InfoWater hydraulic model, used for synchronization between operational systems and modeling platforms.

attributes.name: last_boundary_review_date
attributes.description: Date when the pressure zone boundaries were last reviewed and validated for accuracy, typically as part of GIS updates or hydraulic model recalibration.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pressure zone record was last modified, used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special considerations, historical context, or other relevant information about the pressure zone.

attributes.name: nrw_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of Non-Revenue Water (NRW) within the pressure zone, calculated as the difference between water supplied and billed consumption, used for loss control and efficiency analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 - Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the pressure zone indicating whether it is actively serving customers, temporarily inactive, under maintenance, in emergency mode, or in planned development.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: peak_hour_demand_mgd
attributes.description: Peak hourly water demand in Million Gallons per Day (MGD) for the pressure zone, critical for sizing infrastructure and ensuring adequate pressure during high-demand periods.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: residual_pressure_fire_psi
attributes.description: Minimum residual pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) that must be maintained during fire flow conditions to ensure adequate service to other customers and fire suppression effectiveness.
attributes.references: NFPA 1142 - Standard on Water Supplies for Suburban and Rural Fire Fighting

attributes.name: scada_zone_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Zone Tag
attributes.description: SCADA system tag or point identifier for real-time monitoring of pressure, flow, and operational status within this zone via OSIsoft PI Historian or similar SCADA platforms.

attributes.name: service_area_sq_mi
attributes.description: Geographic area in square miles covered by the pressure zone, used for demand density calculations and infrastructure planning.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: storage_capacity_mg
attributes.description: Total storage capacity in Million Gallons (MG) of all tanks and reservoirs serving the pressure zone, used for emergency supply and pressure stabilization.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: target_pressure_max_psi
attributes.description: Maximum target operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) to prevent infrastructure damage, excessive leakage, and customer service issues.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: target_pressure_min_psi
attributes.description: Minimum target operating pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) that must be maintained throughout the zone to ensure adequate service delivery and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems; EPA Safe Drinking Water Act

attributes.name: ufw_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) within the pressure zone, representing water losses that cannot be attributed to known uses, critical for leak detection and infrastructure assessment.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 - Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: zone_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code or identifier for the pressure zone used in GIS, SCADA, and hydraulic modeling systems.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: zone_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation of the pressure zone used for operational reference and communication.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

attributes.name: zone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pressure zone based on the primary method of pressure maintenance: gravity-fed from elevated storage, pumped from pump stations, combination of both, elevated tank-fed, or booster zone.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 - Computer Modeling of Water Distribution Systems

products.name: dma
products.description: Master record for District Metered Areas (DMAs) — discrete, hydraulically isolated zones of the distribution network used for NRW/UFW monitoring and leakage management. Captures DMA name, boundary description, inlet meter points, outlet meter points, target NRW percentage, minimum night flow (MNF) threshold (GPM), associated pressure zone, GIS polygon boundary, and active status. Core to leakage detection and water loss control programs.
products.reference: IWA District Metered Area; AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the District Metered Area. Primary key for the DMA master record.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: compliance_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_permit. Business justification: DMAs are management units subject to permit conditions for water loss control, NRW reporting requirements, and system efficiency standards. Permits may mandate specific NRW targets and leakage reducti

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pressure zone within which this DMA operates. Pressure zones define areas of similar hydraulic pressure managed by Pressure Reducing Valves (PRVs) and pump stations.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management

attributes.name: average_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Average operating pressure within the DMA measured in Pounds per Square Inch. Pressure management is critical for leakage control; excessive pressure increases leak rates and pipe stress.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management

attributes.name: boundary_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the DMA boundary including street names, landmarks, and physical boundaries used to define the hydraulically isolated zone.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the DMA record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business criticality rating of the DMA based on factors such as population served, infrastructure condition, leakage history, and service area importance. Critical DMAs receive priority for monitoring and maintenance.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: decommissioned_date
attributes.description: Date when the DMA was decommissioned or reconfigured. Null for active DMAs. Used for historical tracking and audit purposes.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: design_flow_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Flow in Million Gallons per Day (MGD)
attributes.description: Design flow capacity for the DMA in Million Gallons per Day. Represents the maximum daily demand the DMA is engineered to supply under normal operating conditions.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the DMA used in operational systems, GIS, and reporting. Typically alphanumeric and unique across the distribution network.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: dma_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the DMA including boundary landmarks, service area characteristics, and any operational notes relevant to leakage management and monitoring.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: dma_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the DMA, often reflecting geographic location or service area (e.g., 'Downtown West DMA', 'Industrial Park Zone 3').
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: dma_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the DMA. Active DMAs are fully operational and monitored; inactive or decommissioned DMAs are no longer in use; planned DMAs are in design phase; under review indicates reconfiguration or audit in progress.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: established_date
attributes.description: Date when the DMA was first established and commissioned for operational monitoring. Represents the start of the DMAs lifecycle.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: gis_polygon_boundary
attributes.description: GIS polygon geometry defining the spatial boundary of the DMA. Typically stored as WKT (Well-Known Text) or reference to GIS layer feature ID for integration with Esri ArcGIS.

attributes.name: inlet_meter_count
attributes.description: Number of inlet flow meters installed at entry points to the DMA. Inlet meters measure total water entering the zone and are critical for NRW calculation.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: isolation_valve_count
attributes.description: Number of isolation valves installed at the DMA boundary. Isolation valves enable hydraulic isolation of the DMA for accurate flow measurement and leakage detection.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management

attributes.name: last_leakage_survey_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent active leakage detection survey conducted within the DMA. Used to track compliance with leakage management programs.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the DMA record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: leakage_detection_frequency_days
attributes.description: Frequency in days at which active leakage detection surveys are conducted within the DMA. High-risk or high-leakage DMAs may be surveyed more frequently.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: main_length_miles
attributes.description: Total length of water mains (distribution pipes) within the DMA measured in miles. Used for calculating leakage per mile of main and infrastructure density metrics.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: minimum_night_flow_threshold_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Night Flow (MNF) Threshold in Gallons per Minute (GPM)
attributes.description: Minimum Night Flow threshold in Gallons per Minute. MNF is the lowest flow rate measured during nighttime hours (typically 2 AM to 4 AM) when legitimate consumption is minimal. Elevated MNF indicates leakage within the DMA.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: next_scheduled_survey_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next active leakage detection survey within the DMA. Used for planning and resource allocation.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, historical context, or any additional information relevant to the DMA management and monitoring.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: outlet_meter_count
attributes.description: Number of outlet flow meters installed at exit points from the DMA. Outlet meters are used in complex DMA configurations where water may flow to adjacent zones.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: population_served
attributes.description: Estimated population served by the DMA. Used for per-capita consumption analysis and demand forecasting.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: prv_count
attributes.description: Number of Pressure Reducing Valves installed within or at the boundary of the DMA. PRVs control pressure to reduce leakage and pipe stress.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management

attributes.name: scada_monitored_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMA is actively monitored by the SCADA system. SCADA-monitored DMAs provide real-time flow, pressure, and alarm data for proactive leakage management.
attributes.references: AWWA M32 Distribution Network Modeling and Management; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: service_connection_count
attributes.description: Total number of active service connections (customer meters) within the DMA. Used for calculating per-connection leakage rates and NRW metrics.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: target_nrw_percentage
attributes.description: Target threshold for Non-Revenue Water as a percentage of total water supplied to the DMA. NRW includes physical losses (leakage) and commercial losses (metering inaccuracies, theft). Typical industry targets range from 10% to 20%.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs; IWA Water Loss Task Force

attributes.name: target_ufw_percentage
attributes.description: Target threshold for Unaccounted-for Water as a percentage of total water supplied. UFW is a broader measure than NRW and includes all water that cannot be accounted for through billing or authorized use.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

products.name: network_valve
products.description: Master record for all distribution network valves including gate valves, butterfly valves, ball valves, and check valves used for flow control and system isolation. Captures valve type, size (inches), manufacturer, installation year, location (GIS coordinates, street address, nearest main reference), pressure zone, DMA, normal operating position (open/closed), number of turns to operate, last exercised date, condition rating, and CMMS asset reference. Critical for isolation analysis (determining minimum valve closures to isolate a pipe segment) and valve exercising programs.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the distribution network valve record. Primary key.

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Valves are procured inventory items with manufacturer specifications. Essential for spare parts management, warranty tracking, equipment standardization programs, and maintenance planning. Manufacture

attributes.name: pipe_main_id

attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id

Pressure zones are geographic areas maintained at specific pressure ranges (measured in Pounds per Square Inch - PSI) to ensure adequate service and prevent pipe bursts. attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: primary_network_asset_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the asset registry record in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Links this valve to IBM Maximo Asset Management for maintenance tracking, work orders, and lifecycle management.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Valve suppliers tracked for approved vendor list management, quality assurance, delivery performance, and warranty management. Essential for procurement compliance and equipment standardization progra

attributes.name: burial_depth_feet
attributes.description: Depth in feet from ground surface to the valve operating nut. Used for excavation planning, valve box sizing, and accessibility assessment. Typical range is 3-8 feet depending on frost line and main depth.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality in which the valve is located. Used for jurisdictional reporting and geographic analysis.

attributes.name: condition_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of the valve's physical condition based on the most recent inspection. Excellent: like new, no defects; Good: minor wear, fully functional; Fair: moderate wear, functional with minor issues; Poor: significant deterioration, may fail soon; Critical: immediate replacement required. Used for risk-based asset management and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) planning.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this valve record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance with data governance policies.

attributes.name: current_position
attributes.description: Actual current position of the valve as of the last field verification or SCADA reading. May differ from normal_position during maintenance, emergencies, or operational adjustments.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: diameter_inches
attributes.description: Nominal diameter of the valve in inches. Critical for hydraulic modeling in Innovyze InfoWater and flow capacity calculations. Common sizes range from 2 to 48 inches in distribution networks.
attributes.references: AWWA C500 Gate Valves for Water and Sewerage Systems

attributes.name: exercising_frequency_months
attributes.description: Planned frequency in months for valve exercising activities. Typically 12 months for standard valves, 6 months for critical isolation valves, and 24 months for low-priority valves. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling in CMMS.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier in the Esri ArcGIS system. Links this valve record to the corresponding GIS feature layer for spatial analysis, map display, and network topology modeling.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the valve was originally installed in the distribution network. Used for age-based asset management, depreciation calculations, and replacement planning under the Capital Improvement Program (CIP).

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the valve was installed. Derived from installation_date for simplified age analysis and reporting when exact date is not required.

attributes.name: is_buried
attributes.description: Indicates whether the valve is buried underground (True) or above ground in a vault or building (False). Buried valves require valve box access and are more difficult to exercise; above-ground valves are more accessible but require weather protection.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: is_motorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the valve is equipped with a motor or actuator for remote operation. True for SCADA-controlled valves; False for manual valves requiring field crew operation.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: last_exercised_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the crew member or contractor who last exercised the valve. Supports accountability and quality assurance in valve maintenance programs.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: last_exercised_date
attributes.description: Date the valve was last exercised (opened and closed through its full range of motion). Regular valve exercising prevents seizing and ensures operability during emergencies. AWWA recommends annual exercising for critical valves.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the valve location in decimal degrees. Used for Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping in Esri ArcGIS, field crew navigation, and spatial analysis.
attributes.references: ISO 6709 Standard Representation of Geographic Point Location

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the valve location in decimal degrees. Used for Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping in Esri ArcGIS, field crew navigation, and spatial analysis.
attributes.references: ISO 6709 Standard Representation of Geographic Point Location

attributes.name: material
attributes.description: Primary construction material of the valve body. Ductile iron is most common for large distribution valves; bronze and brass for smaller service valves; stainless steel for corrosive environments; PVC for low-pressure applications.
attributes.references: AWWA C500 Gate Valves for Water and Sewerage Systems

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this valve record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit requirements, and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: normal_position
attributes.description: Standard operating position of the valve under normal conditions. Critical for hydraulic modeling, isolation planning, and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) monitoring. Most distribution valves are normally open; some isolation and control valves are normally closed or throttled.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special instructions, access restrictions, or historical information about the valve. Examples: 'Requires two-person crew due to tight turns', 'Located in private easement, coordinate access', 'Replaced stem in 2018'.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Valve Operating Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)
attributes.description: Normal operating pressure at the valve location in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Used for hydraulic modeling, pressure zone verification, and valve sizing validation. Typical distribution system pressures range from 40-120 PSI.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the valve in the distribution network. Active valves are in service; inactive valves are temporarily out of service; abandoned valves are no longer used but not removed; removed valves have been physically extracted; planned valves are scheduled for installation.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal code of the valve location. Supports geographic segmentation and service area analysis.

attributes.name: pressure_rating_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Valve Pressure Rating (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)
attributes.description: Maximum rated working pressure of the valve in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI) as specified by the manufacturer. Must exceed operating_pressure_psi with adequate safety margin. Common ratings are 150, 200, 250, and 300 PSI.
attributes.references: AWWA C500 Gate Valves for Water and Sewerage Systems

attributes.name: scada_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag
attributes.description: SCADA system tag identifier for automated valves with remote monitoring and control capability. Links to OSIsoft PI Historian for real-time position monitoring, alarm management, and operational analytics. Only populated for motorized or actuated valves integrated with SCADA.

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province in which the valve is located. Used for regulatory reporting to State Drinking Water Programs and Primacy Agencies.

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Nearest street address or intersection to the valve location. Provides human-readable location reference for field crews, emergency responders, and customer service representatives.

attributes.name: turns_to_close
attributes.description: Number of complete turns required to fully close the valve from the fully open position. Used by field crews during valve exercising programs and emergency isolation procedures. Typical range is 5-50 turns depending on valve size and type.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: useful_life_years
attributes.description: Expected useful life of the valve in years from installation date. Used for depreciation calculations per Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) standards, and for long-term replacement planning. Typical range is 50-75 years for distribution valves.

attributes.name: valve_box_type
attributes.description: Type of valve box or access structure protecting the buried valve. Standard boxes for sidewalk/lawn areas; traffic-rated boxes for roadways; extension boxes for deep valves; vaults for large valves; none for above-ground installations.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: valve_function
attributes.description: Primary operational function of the valve in the distribution network. Isolation valves segment the network for maintenance; control valves regulate flow; pressure reducing valves (PRV) manage pressure zones; check valves prevent backflow; air release valves expel trapped air; blowoff valves drain sections.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: valve_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the valve, typically painted or tagged on the valve in the field. Used by operations and maintenance crews for identification.
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: valve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the valve mechanism. Gate valves provide full flow with minimal pressure drop; butterfly valves are compact and quick-operating; ball valves offer tight shutoff; check valves prevent backflow; plug, cone, and needle valves provide throttling control. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gate|butterfly|ball|check|plug|cone|needle — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M51 Air-Release, Air/Vacuum, and Combination Air Valves

attributes.name: measurement_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical location or asset where the flow measurement was captured (DMA inlet/outlet meter, pump station discharge meter, PRV station meter, or bulk transfer point).
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: metering_meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flow meter device that captured this reading. Links to asset registry for meter calibration history and maintenance records.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.storage_tank. Business justification: The flow_reading product description explicitly states flow measurements are captured at storage tanks. A direct FK to storage_tank identifies which tank's inlet/outlet flow is being measured, enablin

attributes.name: alarm_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flow reading triggered an alarm condition in the SCADA system (e.g., flow exceeds threshold, negative flow, meter communication failure).

attributes.name: alarm_type
attributes.description: Classification of the alarm condition if alarm_flag is true. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: high_flow|low_flow|no_flow|reverse_flow|communication_failure|meter_fault|pressure_deviation|temperature_anomaly|data_gap|validation_failure — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian SCADA Integration Standards

attributes.name: billing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flow reading is used for bulk water billing or wholesale customer invoicing (e.g., inter-utility transfers, industrial bulk customers).
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: calibration_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent meter calibration prior to this reading. Used to assess measurement reliability and schedule recalibration.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for operator notes, validation comments, or explanations of anomalies in the flow reading. Used for audit trail and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the flow reading. Good = validated measurement, Suspect = questionable but not rejected, Bad = failed validation, Estimated = calculated/interpolated value, Manual = operator-entered reading.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: engineering_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the flow reading. GPM = Gallons per Minute, MGD = Million Gallons per Day, CFS = Cubic Feet per Second, LPS = Liters per Second, M3H = Cubic Meters per Hour, M3D = Cubic Meters per Day.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: estimated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the flow value is an estimated or interpolated value rather than a direct meter reading. True when meter communication fails or reading is missing.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used to estimate the flow value when direct measurement is unavailable. None indicates a direct measured value.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: flow_direction
attributes.description: Direction of water flow at the measurement point. Inflow = water entering the zone/DMA, Outflow = water leaving the zone/DMA, Bidirectional = flow can reverse direction.

attributes.name: flow_value
attributes.description: The raw flow measurement value as captured by the meter. Represents instantaneous flow rate or cumulative volume depending on measurement type. Used with engineering_unit to interpret the measurement.

attributes.name: hydraulic_model_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flow reading is used for hydraulic model calibration in Innovyze InfoWater or similar distribution network modeling software.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Time interval in minutes over which the flow measurement was aggregated or averaged. Common values: 15, 30, 60 minutes for SCADA polling intervals.

attributes.name: measurement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the flow measurement: instantaneous (real-time snapshot), cumulative (totalizer reading), average (calculated over interval), peak (maximum in interval), or minimum (lowest in interval).
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: meter_accuracy_percent
attributes.description: The rated accuracy of the flow meter at the time of this reading, expressed as a percentage. Used to calculate measurement uncertainty for water balance calculations.

attributes.name: nrw_calculation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flow reading is included in Non-Revenue Water (NRW) or Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) balance calculations for the associated DMA.

attributes.name: pressure_psi

attributes.name: reading_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the flow measurement was captured by the meter or SCADA system. This is the business event timestamp representing the actual measurement occurrence.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flow reading record was first inserted into the data system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this flow reading record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: scada_tag_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag Name
attributes.description: The SCADA system tag or point identifier that sourced this flow reading. Used for traceability back to the PI Historian or SCADA historian database.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The originating system that captured or recorded the flow measurement. SCADA = Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, AMI = Advanced Metering Infrastructure, MANUAL = operator entry, HISTORIAN = OSIsoft PI Historian, HMI = Human Machine Interface.

attributes.name: temperature_f

attributes.description: Cumulative volume reading from the meter totalizer register. Used to calculate interval consumption by differencing consecutive readings. Typically in gallons or cubic meters.

attributes.name: validated_by
attributes.description: User ID or system process name that performed the validation of this flow reading. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: validation_status

attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: validation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the flow reading was validated or reviewed by an operator or automated validation process.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

products.name: nrw_water_balance
products.description: Analytical and operational record for Non-Revenue Water (NRW) and Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) management per AWWA Free Water Audit methodology. Includes periodic (monthly/annual) water balance calculations per DMA and system-wide: system input volume (MGD), authorized consumption (billed metered, billed unmetered, unbilled authorized), apparent losses (meter inaccuracies, unauthorized consumption), real losses (leakage), NRW volume/percentage, and Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI). Also captures leak detection survey records: survey date, method (acoustic correlator, listening stick, GPR), pipe segment surveyed, length surveyed (feet), leaks found, estimated leak rate (GPM), and survey outcome. SSOT for water loss performance tracking and leakage reduction program management.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Average System Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch - PSI)
attributes.description: Average operating pressure in the distribution system during the audit period, measured in pounds per square inch. Higher pressure increases leakage rates. Used in UARL calculation.

attributes.name: billed_metered_consumption_mg
attributes.description: Volume of water that is metered and billed to customers during the audit period, measured in million gallons. This is the primary revenue-generating component.

attributes.description: Volume of water that is billed to customers but not metered (e.g., flat-rate customers), measured in million gallons. Estimated based on customer count and average usage.

attributes.description: Volume of water consumed but not registered by customer meters due to meter under-registration, measured in million gallons. Typically estimated based on meter age and testing data.

attributes.description: Volume of water lost due to billing system errors, data transfer errors, and accounting mistakes, measured in million gallons. Estimated based on billing system audits.

attributes.description: AWWA Water Audit Software data validity score (0-100) indicating the reliability and accuracy of the input data used in the water balance calculation. Higher scores indicate more reliable audits.

attributes.name: infrastructure_leakage_index
attributes.description: Ratio of Current Annual Real Losses (CARL) to Unavoidable Annual Real Losses (UARL). Dimensionless indicator of how well the distribution system is managed relative to its physical characteristics. ILI < 2 is excellent, 2-4 is good, 4-8 is fair, > 8 is poor.
attributes.references: AWWA Water Audit Method, IWA Best Practice

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this water balance record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Leakage on Service Connections (Million Gallons - MG)
attributes.description: Volume of water lost through leaks on service connections from the main to the customer meter, measured in million gallons. Includes leaks on both utility-owned and customer-owned portions.

attributes.name: leakage_on_storage_tanks_mg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Leakage and Overflow on Storage Tanks (Million Gallons - MG)
attributes.description: Volume of water lost through leaks and overflows at storage tanks and reservoirs, measured in million gallons. Includes structural leaks and operational overflows.

attributes.name: leakage_on_transmission_mains_mg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Leakage on Transmission and Distribution Mains (Million Gallons - MG)
attributes.description: Volume of water lost through leaks and breaks on transmission and distribution mains, measured in million gallons. Includes both reported and unreported leaks.

attributes.name: nrw_percentage
attributes.description: Non-Revenue Water expressed as a percentage of system input volume. Calculated as (NRW Volume / System Input Volume) × 100. Industry benchmark for water loss performance.

attributes.name: nrw_volume_mg
attributes.description: Total volume of water that does not generate revenue for the utility, calculated as system input volume minus billed authorized consumption, measured in million gallons. Key performance indicator for water loss management.

attributes.name: real_losses_mg
attributes.description: Volume of water physically lost from the distribution system through leaks, breaks, and overflows on mains, service connections, and storage tanks, measured in million gallons.

attributes.name: service_connection_count
attributes.description: Total number of active service connections in the system or DMA during the audit period. Used in UARL calculation and for normalizing leakage metrics.

attributes.name: system_input_volume_mg
attributes.description: Total volume of water introduced into the distribution system during the audit period, measured in million gallons. Represents the sum of all water entering the system from treatment plants, wells, and purchased sources.

attributes.name: total_main_length_miles
attributes.description: Total length of transmission and distribution mains in the system or DMA, measured in miles. Used in UARL calculation and for normalizing leakage metrics.

attributes.name: ufw_percentage
attributes.description: Unaccounted-for Water expressed as a percentage of system input volume. Calculated as (UFW Volume / System Input Volume) × 100. Legacy metric still used in some jurisdictions.

attributes.name: ufw_volume_mg
attributes.description: Legacy term for water losses, calculated as system input volume minus authorized consumption, measured in million gallons. Equivalent to water losses in modern AWWA methodology.

attributes.name: unauthorized_consumption_mg
attributes.description: Volume of water consumed through illegal connections, meter tampering, or theft, measured in million gallons. Estimated based on field investigations and industry benchmarks.

attributes.name: unavoidable_annual_real_losses_mg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Unavoidable Annual Real Losses (UARL) (Million Gallons - MG)
attributes.description: Theoretical minimum achievable annual real losses for a well-maintained and well-managed system, calculated based on system characteristics (main length, service connections, pressure). Used as the denominator in ILI calculation.
attributes.references: AWWA Water Audit Method, IWA Best Practice

attributes.name: unbilled_authorized_consumption_mg
attributes.description: Volume of water used for authorized purposes but not billed, such as firefighting, main flushing, street cleaning, and utility operations, measured in million gallons.

attributes.name: water_losses_mg
attributes.description: Total volume of water lost in the distribution system, calculated as system input volume minus authorized consumption, measured in million gallons. Comprises apparent losses and real losses.

domains.name: wastewater
domains.description: Manages wastewater collection, conveyance, and treatment operations including sewer network topology, gravity sewers, force mains, lift stations, manholes, CSO/SSO management, I&I monitoring, FOG program management, industrial user permits (IUP), and NPDES compliance tracking. Supports DMR submissions and biosolids management.
domains.references: EPA CWA, NPDES, WEF Standards, NACWA

products.name: sewer_network
products.description: Master topology of the wastewater collection and conveyance network including gravity sewers, force mains, interceptors, and trunk lines. Captures pipe material, diameter, length, slope, invert elevations, installation year, condition grade, and GIS geometry. Each segment is individually identifiable by upstream/downstream manhole nodes. Serves as the authoritative spatial and hydraulic reference for the sewer system, aligned with Esri ArcGIS Utility Network and Innovyze InfoSWMM/ICM hydraulic models.
products.reference: Sewer Network / Collection System

attributes.name: condition_grade
attributes.description: Current physical condition assessment of the sewer segment based on CCTV inspection, PACP (Pipeline Assessment and Certification Program) scoring, or field evaluation. Drives maintenance and replacement decisions.

attributes.name: coordinate_system

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sewer network record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: criticality_score

attributes.name: hydrogen_sulfide_risk_flag

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the sewer segment was originally installed. Key attribute for asset age analysis, depreciation schedules, and capital improvement program (CIP) prioritization.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent CCTV or physical inspection of the sewer segment. Supports compliance with regulatory inspection frequency requirements and condition assessment programs.
attributes.references: EPA Consent Decree; NASSCO PACP; Internal O&M (Operations and Maintenance) Standards

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this sewer network record. Enables change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: length_feet
attributes.description: Physical length of the sewer segment in feet measured from upstream to downstream node. Used for asset inventory valuation and hydraulic calculations.

attributes.name: lining_installation_date
attributes.description: Date when pipe lining or rehabilitation was completed. Resets the effective age for condition assessment and extends asset useful life.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special conditions, historical context, or field observations relevant to the sewer segment.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sewer segment in the collection network. Active segments are in service; abandoned segments are out of service but not removed.
attributes.references: AWWA Standards; Internal Asset Management Policy

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Legal ownership classification of the sewer segment. Determines maintenance responsibility, regulatory jurisdiction, and capital funding eligibility.
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission; Internal Asset Registry Policy

attributes.name: peak_flow_gpm
attributes.description: Maximum observed or modeled flow rate in Gallons per Minute (GPM) during peak wet weather or high demand periods. Critical for SSO risk assessment.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; Innovyze InfoWater; EPA SSO Rule

attributes.name: replacement_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated current replacement cost of the sewer segment in US Dollars. Used for asset valuation, insurance, and capital improvement program (CIP) budgeting.

attributes.name: root_intrusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether tree root intrusion has been observed or is a known risk for this segment. Common in older vitrified clay and concrete pipes.

attributes.name: segment_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the sewer segment used in GIS systems, field operations, and regulatory reporting. Aligns with Esri ArcGIS feature identifiers.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Data Model; AWWA Standards

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sewer segment by conveyance method and network hierarchy. Gravity sewers use slope for flow; force mains use pumps; interceptors and trunk lines are major collectors.
attributes.references: AWWA Standards; WEF Manual of Practice

attributes.name: slope_percent
attributes.description: Gradient of the sewer pipe expressed as a percentage. Critical for gravity sewer hydraulic performance and self-cleansing velocity calculations.
attributes.references: WEF Manual of Practice; Innovyze InfoWater Hydraulic Model

attributes.name: sso_history_count
attributes.description: Number of Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO) events recorded for this segment. High counts trigger regulatory scrutiny and prioritize capacity upgrades.
attributes.references: EPA SSO Rule; State Water Quality Standards

attributes.name: traffic_impact_level
attributes.description: Assessment of traffic disruption risk if the segment requires excavation or repair. High-traffic segments require special permitting and coordination.
attributes.references: Internal Field Operations Standards; Municipal Right-of-Way Regulations

attributes.name: upstream_invert_elevation_feet
attributes.description: Elevation of the inside bottom of the pipe at the upstream end in feet above mean sea level. Essential for hydraulic grade line analysis and I&I (Inflow and Infiltration) assessment.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Elevation Model; AWWA Standards

Manholes are key access and junction points in the gravity sewer network and are individually tracked for maintenance and I&I assessment.
products.reference: Manhole / Access Structure

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Manhole inspection, rehabilitation, and maintenance costs must be attributed to cost centers for O&M budget management and rate case cost allocation. Utilities organize collection system maintenance b

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.location. Business justification: Manholes are discrete point assets placed within the functional location hierarchy (basin, pressure zone, service territory) used for work order routing, spatial asset management, and field crew dispa

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Manhole rehabilitation uses specific materials (covers, frames, liners, grout) tracked in material master. Linking manholes to material specifications supports maintenance planning, inventory manageme

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: Manholes are infrastructure assets requiring inspection scheduling, condition-based maintenance, capital replacement planning, and asset valuation for rate-setting. Integration with asset registry ena

attributes.name: asset_class_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the asset class or category to which this manhole belongs in the utility's asset hierarchy. Used for financial reporting, depreciation, and capital planning.

attributes.name: basin_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the drainage basin or sewershed that this manhole serves. Used for hydraulic modeling and capacity planning.

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality where the manhole is located. Used for jurisdictional reporting and service area analysis.

attributes.name: confined_space_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the manhole is classified as a permit-required confined space under OSHA regulations. True if the manhole requires a confined space entry permit; false otherwise. Critical for worker safety and entry procedures.

attributes.name: cover_type
attributes.description: Type of cover installed on the manhole. Watertight covers prevent Inflow and Infiltration (I&I); bolted covers provide security; vented covers allow gas release; traffic-rated covers support vehicular loads.
attributes.references: ASTM A48 Standard Specification for Gray Iron Castings

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this manhole record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: depth_feet
attributes.description: Total depth of the manhole from rim elevation to invert elevation, measured in feet. Critical for determining access requirements, safety protocols, and confined space entry procedures.

attributes.name: diameter_inches
attributes.description: Internal diameter of the manhole structure measured in inches. Standard diameters are 48 inches (4 feet) or 60 inches (5 feet) for personnel access.
attributes.references: ASTM C478 Standard Specification for Precast Reinforced Concrete Manhole Sections

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the District Metered Area (DMA) or pressure zone to which this manhole belongs. Used for network segmentation and performance monitoring.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the manhole feature in the utility's GIS system. Used to link asset management data with spatial data layers in ArcGIS or other GIS platforms.

attributes.name: inflow_infiltration_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the manhole has been identified as a source of Inflow and Infiltration (I&I) into the wastewater collection system. True if I&I has been observed or suspected; false otherwise. Used for prioritizing I&I reduction programs.
attributes.references: EPA Capacity Management Operations and Maintenance (CMOM) Program

attributes.name: invert_elevation_feet
attributes.description: Elevation of the lowest point inside the manhole where wastewater flows, measured in feet above a reference datum. Critical for calculating pipe slopes and flow gradients.
attributes.references: NAVD88 North American Vertical Datum of 1988

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent inspection of the manhole. Used to track inspection frequency compliance and schedule future inspections.
attributes.references: NASSCO MACP (Manhole Assessment and Certification Program)

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent maintenance activity was performed on the manhole. Includes cleaning, repairs, or rehabilitation work.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the manhole location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and field navigation.

attributes.name: longitude

attributes.description: Regulatory permit number for the disposition site (land application permit, landfill permit, incinerator air permit, etc.).

attributes.name: dmr_reporting_period
attributes.description: The monthly or quarterly DMR reporting period (YYYY-MM format) to which this batch should be included. Used for automated DMR preparation.

attributes.name: dry_weight_tons
attributes.description: Total dry weight of the biosolids batch in US tons (2,000 lbs). Used for regulatory reporting, disposal tracking, and beneficial use application rate calculations.

attributes.name: exceptional_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this batch meets Exceptional Quality criteria (Class A pathogen reduction, pollutant concentration limits per Table 3, and vector attraction reduction). EQ biosolids have no federal land application restrictions.

attributes.name: fecal_coliform_density_mpn_per_gram
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fecal Coliform Density Most Probable Number (MPN) per Gram Dry Weight
attributes.description: Fecal coliform density in MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis). Class A requires <1,000 MPN/g; Class B requires <2,000,000 MPN/g.

attributes.name: laboratory_analysis_date
attributes.description: Date when laboratory analysis of this batch was completed. Used to verify compliance with monitoring frequency requirements.

attributes.name: lead_concentration_mg_per_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead (Pb) Concentration Milligrams per Kilogram (mg/kg) Dry Weight
attributes.description: Lead concentration in milligrams per kilogram dry weight. Ceiling concentration limit: 840 mg/kg per 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1.

attributes.name: mercury_concentration_mg_per_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mercury (Hg) Concentration Milligrams per Kilogram (mg/kg) Dry Weight
attributes.description: Mercury concentration in milligrams per kilogram dry weight. Ceiling concentration limit: 57 mg/kg per 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1.

attributes.name: nickel_concentration_mg_per_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Nickel (Ni) Concentration Milligrams per Kilogram (mg/kg) Dry Weight
attributes.description: Nickel concentration in milligrams per kilogram dry weight. Ceiling concentration limit: 420 mg/kg per 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes regarding batch production, quality issues, special handling requirements, or other operational observations.

attributes.name: pathogen_class
attributes.description: Classification of pathogen reduction achieved: Class A (unrestricted use, meets PFRP requirements) or Class B (restricted use, meets PSRP requirements) per 40 CFR Part 503.

attributes.name: percent_solids
attributes.description: Percentage of total solids content in the biosolids batch. Typical range: 15-30% for dewatered cake, 90%+ for dried pellets. Critical for vector attraction reduction Option 7 (75% solids minimum).
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 503.33(b)(7) - Vector Attraction Reduction Option 7

attributes.name: ph_value
attributes.description: pH measurement of the biosolids batch. Required for alkaline stabilization processes (pH 12+ for 2 hours minimum per vector attraction reduction Option 6).
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 503.33(b)(6) - Vector Attraction Reduction Option 6

attributes.name: salmonella_density_mpn_per_4_grams
attributes.business_glossary_term: Salmonella Density Most Probable Number (MPN) per 4 Grams Dry Weight
attributes.description: Salmonella sp. bacteria density in MPN per 4 grams of total solids (dry weight basis). Class A requires <3 MPN/4g.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 503.32(a)(3) - Class A Pathogen Requirements

attributes.name: selenium_concentration_mg_per_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Selenium (Se) Concentration Milligrams per Kilogram (mg/kg) Dry Weight
attributes.description: Selenium concentration in milligrams per kilogram dry weight. Ceiling concentration limit: 100 mg/kg per 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1.

attributes.name: total_nitrogen_percent
attributes.description: Total nitrogen content as percentage of dry weight. Important for agronomic application rate calculations and nutrient management planning.

attributes.name: total_phosphorus_percent
attributes.description: Total phosphorus content as percentage of dry weight. Critical for land application planning and nutrient management compliance.

attributes.name: total_potassium_percent
attributes.description: Total potassium content as percentage of dry weight. Used for fertilizer value assessment and agronomic rate calculations.

attributes.name: treatment_process_type
attributes.description: The primary treatment process used to stabilize this biosolids batch. Determines pathogen reduction and vector attraction reduction requirements.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 503.32 - Processes to Significantly Reduce Pathogens (PSRP) and Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP)

attributes.name: vector_attraction_reduction_method
attributes.description: The specific vector attraction reduction option (1-10) applied per 40 CFR Part 503.33. Options include volatile solids reduction, digestion, pH adjustment, moisture reduction, and others.

attributes.name: volatile_solids_reduction_percent
attributes.description: Percentage reduction in volatile solids achieved during treatment. Required for vector attraction reduction Options 1 and 2 (38% minimum reduction).
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 503.33(b)(1) and (b)(2) - Vector Attraction Reduction Options 1 and 2

attributes.name: wet_weight_tons
attributes.description: Total wet weight (as-hauled) of the biosolids batch in US tons. Used for transportation logistics and disposal facility invoicing.

attributes.name: zinc_concentration_mg_per_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Zinc (Zn) Concentration Milligrams per Kilogram (mg/kg) Dry Weight
attributes.description: Zinc concentration in milligrams per kilogram dry weight. Ceiling concentration limit: 7,500 mg/kg per 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1.

attributes.name: weather_conditions

attributes.description: Date when the endpoint was successfully commissioned and began transmitting data to the AMI system. May differ from installation date.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Deployment Guide

attributes.name: communication_frequency_minutes
attributes.description: Configured interval in minutes between endpoint transmissions. Typical values: 15, 30, 60 minutes for hourly reads; 1440 for daily reads.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Configuration Guide

attributes.name: communication_protocol
attributes.description: Network communication protocol used by the endpoint. RF (Radio Frequency) for FlexNet, Cellular for 4G/5G, LoRaWAN for low-power wide-area, NB-IoT for narrowband cellular.
attributes.references: AWWA Manual M47 - Utility Management System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this endpoint record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: data_retention_days
attributes.description: Number of days of interval consumption data stored locally on the endpoint device before being overwritten. Typically 35-45 days.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specifications

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date when the endpoint was removed from service or deactivated. Null for active endpoints.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: decommission_reason
attributes.description: Reason for endpoint decommissioning (e.g., meter replacement, device failure, service disconnection, upgrade to new technology).
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: encryption_algorithm
attributes.description: Cryptographic algorithm used to secure communications between endpoint and collector. AES-128 or AES-256 for encrypted devices.

attributes.name: encryption_key_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the encryption key currently provisioned on the endpoint. Used for secure communication and key rotation management.
attributes.references: NIST SP 800-53 - Security and Privacy Controls

attributes.name: endpoint_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number for the AMI/AMR endpoint device. Used for warranty tracking and device identification.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specifications

attributes.name: endpoint_type
attributes.description: Type of AMI/AMR communication device. ERT (Encoder Receiver Transmitter) for drive-by reading, MXU (Meter Transmit Unit) for fixed network, iPerl for integrated smart meter, Orion for cellular endpoint, Ally for water meter module.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Product Catalog

attributes.name: firmware_version
attributes.description: Current firmware version installed on the endpoint device. Critical for security patches and feature updates.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Firmware Management Guide

attributes.name: geographic_latitude
attributes.description: Latitude coordinate of the endpoint installation location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and network planning.

attributes.name: geographic_longitude
attributes.description: Longitude coordinate of the endpoint installation location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and network planning.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the AMI endpoint was installed and activated in the field. Used for warranty tracking and lifecycle management.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: installation_technician
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the technician who installed the endpoint device. Used for quality tracking and accountability.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: ip_address
attributes.description: IP address assigned to the endpoint device for cellular or IP-based communication protocols. Null for RF-only devices.

attributes.name: last_communication_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful communication received from this endpoint. Used to identify non-communicating devices.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Performance Monitoring Guide

attributes.name: last_firmware_update_date
attributes.description: Date when the endpoint firmware was last updated. Critical for security patch tracking and compliance.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Firmware Management Guide

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this endpoint record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: leak_alert_threshold_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Leak Alert Threshold in Gallons Per Minute (GPM)
attributes.description: Continuous flow threshold in gallons per minute that triggers a leak alert. Typically 0.01 to 0.5 GPM for residential meters.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_detection_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether continuous leak detection monitoring is enabled on this endpoint. True if enabled, False if disabled.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: mac_address
attributes.description: Unique hardware address assigned to the endpoint network interface. Used for device authentication and network routing.

attributes.name: network_node_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the network node or collector that this endpoint communicates with in the AMI network topology.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Network Architecture Guide

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional notes, special instructions, or historical information about the endpoint device.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the endpoint device. Active indicates normal operation, Failed indicates communication or device failure.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Device Management Guide

attributes.name: read_interval_seconds
attributes.description: Interval in seconds at which the endpoint records consumption data internally. Typical values: 900 (15 min), 3600 (hourly), 86400 (daily).
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Configuration Guide

attributes.name: reverse_flow_detected_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether reverse flow has been detected by the endpoint. True if reverse flow detected, False otherwise. May indicate backflow or meter installation error.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: signal_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of communication signal quality. Derived from signal strength and packet success rate.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Performance Monitoring Guide

attributes.name: signal_strength_dbm
attributes.description: Most recent radio signal strength measurement in dBm. Indicates communication quality between endpoint and collector. Typical range -110 to -50 dBm.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Performance Monitoring Guide

attributes.name: tamper_detected_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the most recent tamper event was detected by the endpoint. Null if no tamper has been detected.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: tamper_status
attributes.description: Current tamper detection status reported by the endpoint. Alerts to potential theft, fraud, or unauthorized access.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: warranty_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the manufacturer warranty for the endpoint device expires. Used for replacement planning and cost recovery.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

products.name: read
products.description: Individual meter reading record capturing the register value at a specific point in time for a given meter installation. Stores read date and time, read value (gallons or CCF), read type (AMI automated, AMR drive-by, manual field read, estimated), read source system, reader employee ID (for manual reads), read quality flag, exception code, and whether the read was used for billing. The authoritative transactional record for all meter reads feeding the Oracle CC&B billing cycle.
products.reference: AWWA M6; Oracle CC&B Meter Read Interface

attributes.name: read_id
attributes.description: Primary key for read

attributes.name: ami_endpoint_id

attributes.name: meter_installation_id
