attributes.name: read_route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.read_route. Business justification: Meter reads are collected along defined read routes (for manual, walk-by, or drive-by reading operations). Each read should reference which route it was collected on for operational tracking and route

products.name: interval_consumption
products.description: High-frequency interval consumption data collected from AMI endpoints, typically at 15-minute or hourly intervals. Stores meter installation reference, interval start and end timestamps, consumption volume (gallons), flow rate (GPM), data quality indicator, gap flag, and raw pulse count. Sourced from the AMI head-end system and time-series data historian. Enables leak detection, high-usage alerting, time-of-use analysis, and demand forecasting at sub-daily granularity.
products.reference: Sensus FlexNet AMI Interval Data; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: interval_consumption_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each interval consumption record. Primary key for the interval consumption data product.

attributes.name: ami_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the AMI endpoint device that transmitted this interval data. Corresponds to the Sensus FlexNet endpoint serial number or device identifier.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: cycle_id
attributes.description: Reference to the billing cycle during which this interval occurred. Used to aggregate interval data for billing purposes and time-of-use rate calculations.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing (CC&B) Technical Reference

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Reference to the District Metered Area where this meter is located. Used for Non-Revenue Water (NRW) analysis, pressure zone management, and distribution network optimization.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_detection_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.leak_detection_event. Business justification: interval_consumption already has a leak_detection_flag (BOOLEAN) indicating that a specific interval record exhibits leak-like consumption patterns. When a leak_detection_event is formally raised, the

attributes.name: meter_installation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific meter installation that generated this interval reading. Links to the meter installation registry in the metering domain.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: revenue_accrual_general_ledger_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Revenue Accrual General Ledger Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: AMI interval data enables real-time revenue accrual accounting. Utilities must map interval consumption to GL accounts for unbilled revenue accrual at period-end, supporting accurate financial close p

attributes.name: service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.service_agreement. Business justification: Interval consumption data is the direct basis for billing under a service agreement. Linking interval_consumption to service_agreement enables billing reconciliation, consumption reporting per agreeme

attributes.name: alarm_code
attributes.description: Code indicating any alarm condition detected during this interval. Examples include leak alarm, burst alarm, backflow alarm, low battery alarm, or communication failure alarm. Empty if no alarm condition exists.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: battery_voltage
attributes.description: The battery voltage of the AMI endpoint device at the time of this reading, measured in volts. Used to monitor endpoint health and predict battery replacement needs.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: consumption_volume_gallons
attributes.description: The total volume of water consumed during this interval, measured in gallons. This is the primary consumption metric used for billing, leak detection, and demand analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: data_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates the quality and reliability of this interval reading. Valid readings are directly measured; estimated readings are interpolated due to communication gaps; suspect readings show anomalies; missing indicates no data received; tampered indicates potential meter tampering; overflow indicates meter register overflow.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: estimated_method
attributes.description: The method used to estimate this interval reading if data was missing or invalid. None indicates actual measured data. Other values indicate the estimation algorithm applied.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: flow_rate_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flow Rate in Gallons Per Minute (GPM)
attributes.description: The average flow rate during the interval, measured in gallons per minute. Calculated as consumption volume divided by interval duration. Used for leak detection and high-flow alerting.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: gap_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interval represents a data gap that was filled by estimation or interpolation. True indicates the reading is estimated due to missing data transmission.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: high_usage_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interval exceeded the high-usage threshold for this meter installation. True indicates consumption significantly above normal patterns, potentially indicating irrigation, filling pools, or abnormal usage.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The length of the consumption interval in minutes. Typically 15, 30, or 60 minutes for AMI systems. Used to normalize consumption rates and identify irregular interval lengths.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the consumption interval ended. Represents the end of the measurement period for this interval reading.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the consumption interval began. Represents the beginning of the measurement period for this interval reading.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_detection_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interval triggered a potential leak alert based on continuous low-flow patterns. True indicates sustained consumption suggesting a possible leak.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this interval reading. Used to document anomalies, manual adjustments, or special circumstances affecting this reading.

attributes.name: pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: The water pressure at the meter location during this interval, measured in pounds per square inch. Available from advanced AMI endpoints with integrated pressure sensors. Used for distribution network monitoring and pressure zone analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: processed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this interval reading was processed and loaded into the data warehouse. Used for data pipeline monitoring and audit trails.

attributes.name: pulse_increment_gallons
attributes.description: The volume of water represented by each pulse from the meter encoder, measured in gallons. Varies by meter size and type. Used to convert pulse counts to consumption volumes.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: raw_pulse_count
attributes.description: The raw cumulative pulse count from the meter encoder at the end of this interval. Each pulse represents a fixed volume increment. Used for data validation and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this interval reading was received by the AMI head-end system. Used to calculate transmission latency and identify delayed readings.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: reverse_flow_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether reverse flow was detected during this interval. True indicates water flowing backward through the meter, which may indicate backflow, meter installation issues, or tampering.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: signal_strength_dbm
attributes.description: The radio signal strength of the AMI endpoint transmission, measured in dBm. Used to assess communication quality and identify endpoints with poor connectivity.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The source system that provided this interval reading. Typically Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform or OSIsoft PI Historian. Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: tamper_event_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the type of tamper event detected during this interval, if any. Examples include magnetic interference, tilt detection, removal detection, or reverse flow. Empty if no tamper event detected.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: temperature_fahrenheit
attributes.description: The ambient temperature at the meter location during this interval, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Some AMI endpoints include temperature sensors for freeze detection and consumption correlation analysis.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: transmission_retry_count
attributes.description: The number of transmission attempts required to successfully deliver this interval reading to the AMI collector. Higher retry counts indicate communication challenges.
attributes.references: Sensus FlexNet AMI Platform Technical Specification

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: The current validation status of this interval reading. Pending indicates awaiting validation; validated indicates passed all quality checks; rejected indicates failed validation; under review indicates manual review required.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: validation_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this interval reading was validated or rejected. Used for audit trails and data quality reporting.

attributes.name: zero_consumption_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether zero consumption was recorded during this interval. True indicates no water usage, which may be normal for vacant properties or may indicate meter malfunction.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

products.name: leak_detection_event
products.description: Records all detected consumption anomaly events including suspected leaks, high usage alerts, continuous flow conditions, backflow indicators, and threshold exceedance alerts identified through AMI interval data analysis or monitoring rules. Captures event type (leak, high usage, continuous flow, backflow, threshold exceedance), detection timestamp, meter installation reference, detection method, threshold and actual values, percentage over threshold, estimated volume impact, alert severity, alert status (open, notified, resolved, dismissed), notification history, customer contact log, and resolution outcome. Supports NRW reduction programs, customer notification workflows, proactive service management, and customer service case creation.
products.reference: AWWA Water Loss Control; IWA Water Balance

attributes.name: leak_detection_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the leak detection event record. Primary key.

attributes.name: compliance_violation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_violation. Business justification: Unresolved leaks exceeding state water loss thresholds constitute compliance violations under EPA water loss control programs and state water audit mandates. Utilities must link leak detection events

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Leak events require customer notification and may trigger billing adjustments. Essential for customer service outreach, high-bill investigations, assistance program eligibility, and tracking notificat

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Reference to the District Metered Area where the leak was detected. Used for geographic analysis and NRW reduction program targeting.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: high_usage_alert_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.high_usage_alert. Business justification: In water utility operations, a high_usage_alert (consumption exceeding threshold) is frequently the precursor event that triggers a leak_detection_event investigation. The leak_detection_event should

attributes.name: meter_installation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the meter installation where the leak was detected. Links to the meter installation registry.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.premise. Business justification: Leaks occur at premises and may indicate infrastructure issues. Required for correlating leak frequency with premise characteristics, prioritizing premise-level infrastructure upgrades, and tracking p

attributes.name: primary_leak_ami_device_ami_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Reference to the AMI device (Sensus FlexNet endpoint or similar) that generated the interval data used for leak detection. Links to AMI device registry.
attributes.references: AWWA M47 Instrumentation and Control of Water Supply Systems

attributes.name: service_address_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service address where the leak was detected. Links to customer service location registry.

attributes.name: service_line_id

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the work order created to investigate or repair the detected leak. Links to asset management work order system.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: alert_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the leak event based on estimated volume, duration, and potential impact. Used to prioritize response and customer outreach.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: billing_adjustment_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this leak event qualifies for a customer billing adjustment under utility leak adjustment policy. True indicates eligibility for adjustment consideration.

attributes.name: confidence_score
attributes.description: Algorithmic confidence score (0-100) indicating the likelihood that the detected anomaly represents a true leak. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in detection accuracy.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: continuous_flow_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator that the leak was detected through continuous flow analysis (flow detected 24 hours without interruption). True indicates continuous flow was the detection trigger.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this leak detection event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: customer_notification_date
attributes.description: Date when the customer was notified about the detected leak event. Used for tracking notification timeliness and customer service metrics.

attributes.name: customer_notified_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the customer has been notified of the detected leak event. True indicates notification has been sent.

attributes.name: detection_algorithm_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the leak detection algorithm or software that identified this event. Used for algorithm performance tracking and continuous improvement.

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: Method or technique used to identify the leak event. Indicates whether detection was automated (AMI interval analysis, continuous flow flag, minimum night flow anomaly) or manual (acoustic sensor, field inspection, customer report).
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the leak was first detected by the AMI system or monitoring algorithm. Principal business event timestamp for this event.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: estimated_leak_volume_gallons_per_day
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Leak Volume in Gallons Per Day (GPD)
attributes.description: Estimated daily water loss volume attributed to the detected leak, measured in gallons per day. Calculated from interval consumption data or continuous flow analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: estimated_total_loss_gallons
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Total Water Loss in Gallons
attributes.description: Total estimated water loss volume from leak start to resolution, measured in gallons. Calculated as leak volume per day multiplied by duration. Contributes to Non-Revenue Water (NRW) and Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) metrics.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: flow_threshold_value
attributes.description: The flow rate threshold value (in gallons per minute or GPM) that was exceeded to trigger the leak detection alert. Used for continuous flow and threshold-based detection methods.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: investigation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for field technician or customer service representative notes regarding leak investigation, customer interaction, or resolution details.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this leak detection event record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: leak_duration_hours
attributes.description: Estimated or measured duration of the leak event from detection timestamp to resolution or current time if unresolved, measured in hours.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_location_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the suspected or confirmed leak location (e.g., service line, toilet, irrigation system, water heater). Provides context for leak source and repair scope.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the leak detection event. Tracks progression from initial detection through investigation, customer notification, and resolution.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: leak_type
attributes.description: Classification of the leak by type or source. Helps categorize leak patterns and target customer education programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: service_line|meter|toilet|faucet|irrigation|water_heater|pool|unknown — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: minimum_night_flow_anomaly_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator that the leak was detected through minimum night flow analysis showing abnormal consumption during low-usage hours (typically 2 AM - 4 AM). True indicates MNF anomaly detection.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Communication channel used to notify the customer about the leak event. Tracks preferred and actual notification delivery method.

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date when the leak event was resolved or closed. Used to calculate response time and track Non-Revenue Water (NRW) reduction program effectiveness.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome or resolution status of the leak detection event. Indicates whether the leak was confirmed and repaired, determined to be a false positive, or remains pending.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

products.name: high_usage_alert
products.description: Operational alert record generated when a meter's consumption exceeds a defined threshold relative to historical baseline, seasonal norms, or absolute volume limits. Stores alert generation timestamp, meter installation reference, alert type (high consumption, continuous flow, backflow suspected), threshold value, actual consumption value, percentage over threshold, alert status (open, notified, resolved, dismissed), customer contact attempt log, and resolution notes. Feeds customer service workflows in Microsoft Dynamics 365.
products.reference: AWWA AMI Best Practices; Customer Notification Protocols

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the high usage alert record. Primary key.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.premise. Business justification: High usage alerts analyzed by premise type for pattern detection. Required for identifying systemic issues by building type, seasonal usage anomalies, and targeting conservation messaging to specific

attributes.name: primary_high_ami_device_ami_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the AMI endpoint device (Sensus FlexNet or similar) that generated the consumption data triggering this alert. Used for device diagnostics and data quality validation.
attributes.references: AWWA Manual M47 - Capital Project Delivery

attributes.name: service_address_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.service_address. Business justification: High usage alerts tied to physical locations for field investigation. Essential for dispatching field crews, correlating alerts with address characteristics, and geographic pattern analysis for leak d

attributes.name: service_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.service_line. Business justification: High usage alerts are investigated at the service line level — field crews need the physical service line asset reference for inspection and repair dispatch. high_usage_alert has premise_id but not se

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.work_order. Business justification: High usage alerts requiring physical meter or service line investigation generate asset work orders (distinct from the service.order already linked). Water utilities dispatch field crews via asset wor

attributes.name: actual_consumption_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the actual consumption value. Gallons, cubic feet, and cubic meters represent volume; GPM (Gallons per Minute) and MGD (Million Gallons per Day) represent flow rate.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: actual_consumption_value
attributes.description: The measured consumption value during the detection period that triggered the alert. Represents the actual usage that exceeded the threshold.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: alert_generated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alert was generated by the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) or analytics system. Represents the moment the threshold breach was detected.
attributes.references: AWWA Manual M47 - Capital Project Delivery

attributes.name: alert_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique alert number used for tracking and customer communication. Format: HUA-XXXXXXXXXX.

attributes.name: alert_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the alert based on variance magnitude and potential impact. Low indicates minor variance; medium indicates moderate concern; high indicates significant issue requiring prompt attention; critical indicates emergency condition requiring immediate response.

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the alert. Open indicates newly generated; notified means customer has been contacted; acknowledged means customer confirmed receipt; investigating indicates active review; resolved means issue addressed; dismissed means no action required; false positive indicates erroneous alert. attributes.description: Classification of the high usage alert based on consumption pattern analysis. High consumption indicates volume exceeds baseline; continuous flow suggests uninterrupted usage; backflow suspected indicates reverse flow detection; leak detected flags potential infrastructure failure; abnormal pattern identifies irregular usage; threshold exceeded indicates absolute limit breach.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: baseline_consumption_value
attributes.description: Historical average or expected consumption value used as the comparison baseline for this alert. May be calculated from seasonal norms, customer history, or similar account profiles.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: customer_notified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has been notified about this high usage alert. True means notification sent; False means no notification sent yet.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or method that provided the consumption data used to generate this alert. AMI interval data represents 15-minute or hourly reads; AMI daily read represents once-per-day automated read; manual read represents field technician reading; estimated read represents calculated value; SCADA flow data represents distribution network monitoring; analytics engine represents derived calculation.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: detection_period_end_timestamp
attributes.description: End of the time window during which the high usage condition was detected. Used to define the consumption analysis interval.

attributes.name: detection_period_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Beginning of the time window during which the high usage condition was detected. Used to define the consumption analysis interval.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: estimated_revenue_impact_amount
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact of the high usage condition, representing potential lost revenue or customer billing adjustment. Positive values indicate revenue at risk; negative values indicate customer credits issued. Null if not calculated.

attributes.name: estimated_water_loss_gallons
attributes.description: Estimated volume of water lost or wasted due to the condition that triggered this alert, measured in gallons. Used for Non-Revenue Water (NRW) and Unaccounted-for Water (UFW) analysis. Null if not applicable or not calculated.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: first_notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the first customer notification was sent for this alert. Null if customer has not been notified.

attributes.name: investigation_started_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when investigation of this alert began. Null if investigation has not started.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this alert record was most recently updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the system user or automated process that last modified this alert record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: notification_count
attributes.description: Total number of notification attempts made to the customer regarding this alert. Includes all channels and retries.

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Primary communication channel used to notify the customer about this alert. Email, SMS, and mobile app represent digital channels; phone call represents voice contact; postal mail represents physical correspondence; customer portal represents self-service access; none indicates no notification sent. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: email|sms|phone_call|postal_mail|mobile_app|customer_portal|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: resolution_category
attributes.description: Classification of the root cause or resolution outcome for this alert. Customer leak repaired indicates customer-side plumbing issue fixed; utility leak repaired indicates utility infrastructure issue fixed; meter malfunction indicates faulty meter; seasonal usage indicates expected variance; customer behavior change indicates legitimate usage increase; irrigation system and pool filling indicate specific high-volume activities; construction activity indicates temporary usage spike; false alarm indicates erroneous alert; other indicates miscellaneous resolution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: customer_leak_repaired|utility_leak_repaired|meter_malfunction|seasonal_usage|customer_behavior_change|irrigation_system|pool_filling|construction_activity|false_alarm|other — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the investigation findings, actions taken, and resolution details for this alert. Provides context for future reference and audit trail.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this alert was resolved or closed. Null if alert remains open or under investigation.

attributes.name: service_order_created_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a field service order was created in response to this alert. True means service order generated; False means no service order created.

attributes.name: suppression_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alert was suppressed from customer notification due to business rules (e.g., customer opted out, account in dispute, recent similar alert). True means suppressed; False means not suppressed.

attributes.name: suppression_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why this alert was suppressed from customer notification. Null if alert was not suppressed.

attributes.name: threshold_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the threshold value. Gallons and cubic feet/meters represent volume; GPM (Gallons per Minute) and MGD (Million Gallons per Day) represent flow rate; percent represents variance from baseline.
attributes.references: AWWA M6 Water Meters - Selection, Installation, Testing, and Maintenance

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The defined limit or baseline value that was exceeded to trigger this alert. May represent absolute volume, flow rate, or percentage variance depending on alert configuration.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

attributes.name: variance_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage by which actual consumption exceeded the threshold value. Calculated as ((actual - threshold) / threshold) * 100. Positive values indicate over-threshold conditions.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs

This is the authoritative SSOT for all physical assets — the IBM Maximo asset master and SAP PM equipment master both synchronize to this record.

attributes.name: asset_tag
attributes.description: Physical asset tag number (barcode, QR code, or RFID label) affixed to the asset in the field. Used by field technicians for asset identification during inspections, maintenance, and inventory audits. Corresponds to the Maximo asset tag field.

attributes.name: asset_type

attributes.name: capacity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the rated_capacity field. attributes.references: AWWA Standards; EPA Drinking Water Standards; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: condition_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal condition assessment performed on the asset. Used to determine assessment currency and schedule the next inspection cycle. Condition assessments may be visual inspections, CCTV surveys, vibration analysis, or other diagnostic methods.
attributes.references: AWWA Asset Management Guidance; ISO 55001; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: condition_grade
attributes.description: Standardized condition rating of the asset based on the most recent condition assessment, using a 1-5 scale where 1=Excellent/New, 2=Good, 3=Fair, 4=Poor, 5=Very Poor/Failed. Aligned with AWWA and WEF condition assessment frameworks. Drives maintenance prioritization and renewal planning.
attributes.references: AWWA Asset Management Guidance; WEF Asset Management; ISO 55001; EPA Asset Management for Water Systems

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the asset record was first created in the enterprise asset registry. Provides audit trail for record provenance and data lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; Data Governance Best Practices

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Risk-based criticality classification of the asset based on consequence of failure analysis (CoFA). 'critical' assets have the highest consequence of failure impacting public health, regulatory compliance, or major service disruption. Used to prioritize maintenance resources, Capital Improvement Program (CIP) investments, and emergency response planning. Aligned with AWWA risk and resilience assessment methodology.
attributes.references: AWWA Risk and Resilience Management (ANSI/AWWA J100); America's Water Infrastructure Act (AWIA) Section 2013; ISO 55001

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was permanently decommissioned, retired, or removed from service. Null for active assets. Used for asset lifecycle reporting, fixed asset register reconciliation, and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) tracking. Triggers write-off in SAP FI/CO fixed asset module.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; SAP ERP FI Asset Accounting; GASB Statement No. 34

attributes.name: diameter_mm
attributes.description: Nominal diameter of the asset in millimeters. For pipes and valves, this is the internal bore diameter. For pumps, this is the discharge diameter. Used for hydraulic capacity calculations, spare parts specification, and network modeling in Innovyze InfoWater.

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the asset above mean sea level in meters. Critical for hydraulic modeling, pressure zone assignment, and gravity-fed system design. Used in Innovyze InfoWater hydraulic models and Esri ArcGIS 3D network analysis.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; Innovyze InfoWater; AWWA Distribution System Standards

attributes.name: expected_useful_life_years
attributes.description: The estimated total useful life of the asset in years as defined by engineering standards, manufacturer specifications, or utility policy. Used for depreciation calculations, Capital Improvement Program (CIP) planning, and asset renewal forecasting. Aligns with GASB Statement No. 34 infrastructure reporting requirements.
attributes.references: GASB Statement No. 34; GAAP; AWWA Asset Management Guidance; ISO 55001

attributes.name: functional_location
attributes.description: Hierarchical functional location code representing the physical or functional position of the asset within the utility's infrastructure (e.g., WTP-PUMP-STATION-01-PUMP-03). Mirrors the SAP PM Functional Location (FLOC) structure and IBM Maximo Location field. Used for structured asset hierarchy navigation and maintenance cost allocation.
attributes.references: SAP ERP PM Functional Location; IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: The unique feature identifier for this asset in the Esri ArcGIS geographic information system. Enables spatial queries, network tracing, and hydraulic model integration via Innovyze InfoWater. Used for field crew navigation and infrastructure mapping.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; Innovyze InfoWater; AWWA GIS Standards

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was physically installed and placed into service at its current location. Used as the baseline for age calculations, depreciation schedules, warranty period tracking, and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. Sourced from IBM Maximo installation date field.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; GAAP; GASB Statement No. 34; ISO 55001

attributes.name: is_lead_service_line
attributes.description: Indicates whether this asset is a lead service line or contains lead components. Critical for compliance with the EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) which requires utilities to inventory and replace lead service lines. True = confirmed lead service line; False = non-lead or unknown.
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR); Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA); EPA LCRR Service Line Inventory Requirements

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recently completed maintenance activity (preventive or corrective) performed on this asset. Used to calculate maintenance intervals, identify overdue assets, and support compliance reporting for regulatory-mandated maintenance activities.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the asset record in the enterprise asset registry. Used for change tracking, data synchronization with IBM Maximo and SAP PM, and audit trail maintenance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; Data Governance Best Practices; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the asset location in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS mapping, field crew navigation, spatial analysis, and hydraulic network modeling in Innovyze InfoWater. Sourced from Esri ArcGIS asset layer.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; WGS84 Geodetic Datum; Innovyze InfoWater

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the asset location in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS mapping, field crew navigation, spatial analysis, and hydraulic network modeling in Innovyze InfoWater. Sourced from Esri ArcGIS asset layer.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; WGS84 Geodetic Datum; Innovyze InfoWater

attributes.name: maintenance_strategy
attributes.description: The primary maintenance approach applied to this asset as defined in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). 'preventive' indicates time-based scheduled maintenance; 'predictive' indicates condition-monitoring-based maintenance; 'condition_based' indicates maintenance triggered by condition thresholds; 'run_to_failure' is applied to non-critical, easily replaceable assets.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001 Asset Management; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: manufacture_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was manufactured by the OEM. May differ from installation date for assets stored in inventory before deployment. Used for age-based condition assessment and manufacturer warranty calculations.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: maximo_asset_num
attributes.description: The asset number as assigned and maintained in IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS). This is the operational cross-reference key used by maintenance crews and work order management. Must be unique within the Maximo instance.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the next scheduled preventive maintenance activity is due for this asset. Derived from the PM schedule and last maintenance date. Used for maintenance planning, resource scheduling, and compliance tracking in IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle state of the asset. 'in_service' indicates the asset is active and performing its intended function. 'standby' indicates the asset is available but not currently operating. 'out_of_service' indicates the asset is temporarily removed from service for maintenance or repair. 'decommissioned' indicates permanent retirement. Drives maintenance scheduling and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; ISO 55001 Asset Management; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: pipe_material
attributes.description: Material composition of the asset (e.g., Ductile Iron, PVC, HDPE, Cast Iron, Concrete, Stainless Steel, Copper). Critical for corrosion risk assessment, Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR) compliance, Cured-in-Place Pipe (CIPP) rehabilitation planning, and remaining useful life estimation. Applicable primarily to pipe and fitting assets.
attributes.references: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR); AWWA Standards; Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA)

attributes.name: power_rating_kw
attributes.description: Nameplate power rating of the asset in kilowatts (kW). Applicable to pumps, blowers, motors, generators, and other electrical equipment. Used for energy consumption analysis, Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) sizing, electrical load planning, and OPEX budgeting.
attributes.references: AWWA Energy Management Guidance; IBM Maximo Asset Management; OSHA Electrical Standards

attributes.name: pressure_zone
attributes.description: The hydraulic pressure zone or District Metered Area (DMA) in which the asset is located. Used for pressure management, Non-Revenue Water (NRW) analysis, and distribution network operations. Aligns with Innovyze InfoWater zone definitions and GIS pressure zone polygons.
attributes.references: Innovyze InfoWater; AWWA Distribution System Standards; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: rated_capacity
attributes.description: The manufacturer-rated operational capacity of the asset expressed in the appropriate unit of measure (see capacity_unit field). For pumps: Gallons per Minute (GPM); for treatment units: Million Gallons per Day (MGD); for tanks: gallons. Used for capacity planning, hydraulic modeling, and performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: AWWA Standards; Innovyze InfoWater; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: replacement_cost
attributes.description: Current estimated cost to replace the asset with a new equivalent unit in US dollars. Updated periodically based on market pricing and engineering estimates. Used for Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budgeting, insurance valuation, and risk-based asset management decision-making.
attributes.references: AWWA Asset Management Guidance; ISO 55001; GASB Statement No. 34

attributes.name: sap_equipment_num
attributes.description: The equipment number assigned in SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) module. Used for integration with SAP FI/CO for depreciation, CAPEX/OPEX tracking, and maintenance cost postings. Enables bidirectional synchronization between SAP PM and the asset registry.
attributes.references: SAP ERP PM Module; GAAP; GASB Statement No. 34

attributes.name: scada_tag
attributes.description: The Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) tag name used to identify this asset's data point(s) in the OSIsoft PI Historian system. Enables linkage between the physical asset registry and real-time operational data streams for performance monitoring, alarm management, and predictive maintenance analytics.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; SCADA System Integration Standards; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: serial_num
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer to this specific asset unit. Used for warranty claims, recall tracking, and precise asset identification when multiple identical units exist. Sourced from IBM Maximo serial number field.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; SAP ERP PM Equipment Master

attributes.name: warranty_expiry_date

attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; SAP ERP PM Warranty Management

attributes.name: emergency_response_actions

attributes.name: failure_cause

attributes.name: failure_criticality_score
attributes.description: Calculated criticality score based on failure severity, service impact, and asset importance (typically 1-100 scale).

attributes.name: failure_date

attributes.name: failure_effect

attributes.name: failure_mode

attributes.name: failure_number

attributes.name: failure_severity

attributes.name: failure_status

attributes.name: mttr_hours

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: overflow_volume_gallons

attributes.name: pressure_drop_psi

attributes.name: production_loss_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Production Loss in Million Gallons per Day (MGD)
attributes.description: Estimated water production capacity lost due to the failure, measured in Million Gallons per Day.

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date
attributes.description: Date when regulatory agencies were notified of the failure event, if applicable.

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the failure event requires notification to regulatory agencies (EPA, state primacy agency).
attributes.references: EPA SDWA and CWA Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: repair_cost_estimate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Repair Cost in US Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated total cost to repair or replace the failed asset, including labor, materials, and contractor costs.

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date when the failure was fully resolved and the asset was restored to normal operation.

attributes.name: root_cause_analysis_completed_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a formal root cause analysis (RCA) has been completed for this failure event.

attributes.name: root_cause_analysis_findings
attributes.description: Detailed findings and conclusions from the root cause analysis investigation, including contributing factors and systemic issues identified.

attributes.name: service_interruption_flag

attributes.name: sso_event_flag

attributes.name: warranty_claim_flag

products.name: asset_meter
products.description: Tracks operational meters, counters, and their reading history for asset condition and usage monitoring — distinct from customer billing meters (owned by the metering domain). Examples include pump run-hours, motor starts, valve cycle counts, flow totalizers (MGD), pressure transducers (PSI), and vibration sensors. Captures meter type, unit of measure, current reading, rollover value, calibration status, and historical reading records (reading date/time, value, source — manual or SCADA/PI Historian automated, inspector ID, delta from previous reading). Feeds meter-based PM triggers, tracks asset utilization trends, and supports predictive maintenance analytics. Integrates with OSIsoft PI Historian.
products.reference: IBM Maximo Asset Meter / OSIsoft PI Tag

attributes.name: asset_meter_id

attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter object; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: location_id

attributes.name: metering_meter_id
attributes.description: The native meter identifier from IBM Maximo Asset Management CMMS (METERNAME or internal Maximo meter key). Used for system-of-record traceability and bidirectional synchronization between the Silver Layer and Maximo.

attributes.name: primary_asset_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent physical asset (pump, motor, valve, pipe segment, vehicle, etc.) to which this operational meter or counter is attached. Links to the asset master record in the asset domain.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Asset object; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: process_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.process_unit. Business justification: Asset meters installed on treatment process units (run-hour meters on filters, flow meters on clarifiers) must reference the process_unit for SCADA integration, PM trigger management, and process perf

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Regulatory meters (is_regulatory_meter=true) are designated for specific monitoring requirements under NPDES, SDWA, or state permits. Tracing each regulatory meter to its governing requirement support

attributes.name: sampling_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.quality_sampling_point. Business justification: Operational meters (flow, pressure, chlorine residual) are co-located with or serve as quality sampling points. Water utilities integrate meter readings with sampling point data for distribution syste

attributes.name: alarm_high_threshold
attributes.description: The upper alarm threshold value for this meter. When the reading exceeds this value, a SCADA or CMMS alarm is triggered. For example, high vibration alarm at 0.5 in/s for a pump motor. Supports integration with SCADA HMI alarm management.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian — Tag alarm limits; SCADA/HMI alarm management; AWWA O&M

attributes.name: alarm_low_threshold
attributes.description: The lower alarm threshold value for this meter. When the reading falls below this value, a SCADA or CMMS alarm is triggered. For example, low flow alarm at 0.1 MGD for a treatment process feed pump.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian — Tag alarm limits; SCADA/HMI alarm management; AWWA O&M

attributes.name: average_reading_rate
attributes.description: The average rate of change per day for this meter, calculated and stored by the CMMS during reading entry (not a derived KPI — stored as a CMMS field used for PM trigger forecasting). For example, average run-hours per day for a pump. Used by meter-based PM triggers to forecast next maintenance due date.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.AVGCALCMETHOD / average reading; AWWA Asset Management

attributes.name: avg_calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used by the CMMS to compute the average_reading_rate. SLIDING_WINDOW: rolling average over a configurable number of recent readings. FIXED_PERIOD: average over a fixed calendar period. LAST_READING: uses only the most recent reading interval.

attributes.name: calibration_interval_days
attributes.description: The required frequency of calibration expressed in calendar days. Used to compute next_calibration_date from last_calibration_date and to schedule calibration work orders in IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; AWWA; EPA measurement standards

attributes.name: calibration_status
attributes.description: Current calibration status of the meter instrument. CALIBRATED: within valid calibration period. DUE: calibration due within the next calibration_interval_days. OVERDUE: calibration date has passed without recalibration. IN_PROGRESS: currently being calibrated. NOT_REQUIRED: meter type does not require formal calibration (e.g., simple cycle counters).
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management — Measurement Equipment Calibration; AWWA; EPA measurement standards

attributes.name: calibration_tolerance
attributes.description: Acceptable measurement tolerance or accuracy specification for this meter expressed in the meter's unit of measure. Readings outside this tolerance trigger recalibration. For example, ±0.5 PSI for a pressure transducer or ±0.01 MGD for a flow totalizer.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; AWWA M6 Water Meters; EPA measurement accuracy standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the asset meter record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; GASB; GAAP audit trail requirements

attributes.name: current_reading
attributes.description: The most recent recorded value of the meter or counter as of the last_reading_date. For CONTINUOUS meters this is the cumulative total; for GAUGE meters this is the last observed point-in-time value. Principal quantitative fact for this MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.LASTREADINGDATE / LASTREADING; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the meter was permanently removed from service and retired. Null for active meters. Used for lifecycle reporting and asset history.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Asset retirement; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the meter was physically installed on the asset. Used to calculate meter age, warranty expiry, and to establish the baseline reading at installation.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Asset installation date; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: is_regulatory_meter
attributes.description: Indicates whether readings from this meter are used in regulatory compliance reporting (e.g., EPA NPDES Discharge Monitoring Reports, Safe Drinking Water Act compliance, Monthly Operating Reports). True = regulatory-grade meter subject to calibration and data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES (CWA); Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA); EPA DMR; State Primacy Agencies

attributes.name: last_calibration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the meter was most recently calibrated and certified as accurate. Critical for regulatory compliance where metered values (e.g., flow, pressure, chemical dosing) are used in EPA/NPDES reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; EPA NPDES Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR); AWWA

attributes.name: last_reading_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Meter Reading Date and Time
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent meter reading captured, whether from SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian automated feed or manual entry in IBM Maximo. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.LASTREADINGDATE; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: location_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the physical location where the meter is installed on the asset, e.g., 'Discharge side of Pump 3 at WTP Building A', 'Inlet valve actuator shaft'. Supplements the parent asset location for field technician navigation.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Location description; AWWA Asset Management

attributes.name: measurement_unit
attributes.description: Engineering unit of measure for the meter reading, e.g., HOURS (run-hours), STARTS (motor starts), CYCLES (valve cycles), MGD (Million Gallons per Day), GPM (Gallons per Minute), PSI (Pounds per Square Inch), NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units), RPM, DEGREES_F, INCHES. Aligns with OSIsoft PI Historian tag engineering units.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian — Tag Engineering Units; AWWA M6; ISO 80000-1 Quantities and Units

attributes.name: meter_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the meter or counter, e.g., 'Pump 3 Run Hours', 'Valve 12 Cycle Count', 'Influent Flow Totalizer'. Used for display in CMMS work orders and PM triggers.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.DESCRIPTION; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: meter_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier for the meter as assigned in IBM Maximo CMMS or SAP PM. Used for cross-system reference and field identification. Distinct from customer billing meter numbers managed by the Metering domain.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.METERNAME; SAP PM Equipment Master

attributes.name: meter_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the meter. ACTIVE: in service and collecting readings. INACTIVE: temporarily not in use. RETIRED: permanently decommissioned. SUSPENDED: readings paused (e.g., asset out of service). PENDING_CALIBRATION: due for or undergoing calibration.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter lifecycle; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: meter_type
attributes.description: Classification of the meter per IBM Maximo meter type taxonomy. CONTINUOUS: accumulating counter that never resets (e.g., run-hours, cycle counts, flow totalizer). GAUGE: point-in-time measurement that can go up or down (e.g., PSI, vibration amplitude, temperature). CHARACTERISTIC: qualitative or categorical observation (e.g., condition rating, oil color).
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.METERTYPE; AWWA M6 Water Meters

attributes.name: next_calibration_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date by which the meter must next be calibrated to maintain measurement accuracy and regulatory compliance. Drives calibration work order generation in IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; EPA NPDES DMR; IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS)

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI Historian tag identifier associated with this meter for automated SCADA data ingestion. Enables direct linkage between the CMMS meter record and the PI Historian time-series data stream. Null if the meter is not integrated with PI Historian.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian — Tag configuration; SCADA integration standards

attributes.name: pm_trigger_interval
attributes.description: The recurring interval of meter units between successive PM work order generations. For example, every 500 run-hours or every 1000 valve cycles. Works in conjunction with pm_trigger_threshold for ongoing PM scheduling.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — PM Meter Trigger Interval; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: pm_trigger_threshold
attributes.description: The meter reading value at which a Preventive Maintenance (PM) work order is automatically generated. For example, a pump PM triggered every 2000 run-hours. Core field enabling meter-based PM scheduling in IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — PM Meter Trigger; AWWA Asset Management; ISO 55001

attributes.name: previous_reading
attributes.description: The meter reading value recorded immediately prior to the current reading. Used to calculate consumption delta between readings and to detect anomalous jumps or rollover events.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter history; AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: previous_reading_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Previous Meter Reading Date and Time
attributes.description: Timestamp of the meter reading that preceded the current reading. Used in conjunction with previous_reading to compute usage rate and validate reading intervals.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter history; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: reading_frequency
attributes.description: Expected frequency at which meter readings are collected. CONTINUOUS: real-time SCADA/PI Historian streaming. HOURLY/DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY: scheduled batch collection. ON_DEMAND: readings taken only when required (e.g., during inspections or work orders).
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — PM frequency; OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA O&M guidance

attributes.name: reading_range_max
attributes.description: Maximum valid reading value for this meter as defined by the instrument's operating range or process design limits. Readings above this value are flagged as suspect or trigger alarms. For example, 150 PSI maximum for a distribution pressure transducer.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter range; OSIsoft PI Historian tag limits; AWWA

attributes.name: reading_range_min
attributes.description: Minimum valid reading value for this meter as defined by the instrument's operating range or process design limits. Readings below this value are flagged as suspect. For example, 0 PSI minimum for a pressure transducer.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter range; OSIsoft PI Historian tag limits; AWWA

attributes.name: reading_source
attributes.description: The system or method by which the current meter reading was captured. SCADA: from Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system. PI_HISTORIAN: from OSIsoft PI Historian automated feed. MANUAL: entered manually by a technician in IBM Maximo. AMI: from Advanced Metering Infrastructure. CMMS_IMPORT: batch import from CMMS. FIELD_DEVICE: direct PLC/RTU feed.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS); SCADA/PLC integration; AWWA

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, technician observations, or special instructions related to this meter. For example, notes about known reading anomalies, temporary bypass conditions, or pending replacement. Sourced from IBM Maximo meter remarks field.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter remarks; AWWA O&M documentation

attributes.name: rollover_value
attributes.description: The maximum value the meter counter can reach before rolling over to zero. Applicable to CONTINUOUS meters with fixed-digit displays (e.g., 99999.9 hours). Used to correctly compute cumulative usage across rollover events. Null if the meter has no rollover limit.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) — Meter.ROLLOVER; AWWA M6 Water Meters

attributes.references: SAP ERP PM — Measuring Point (IMPTT); SAP PM Integration

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer's serial number uniquely identifying the physical meter instrument. Used for warranty claims, calibration certificates, and asset tracking.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the asset meter record was most recently modified in the enterprise data platform. Used for change tracking, incremental data loads, and audit compliance. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

domains.name: compliance
domains.description: Regulatory compliance management including permit tracking (NPDES, IUP, state primacy agency permits), MOR/DMR preparation and submission, violation management, enforcement action tracking, audit trails, environmental reporting, SDWA and CWA compliance, CCR publication tracking, and regulatory correspondence. Ensures adherence to all federal, state, and local water and wastewater regulations.

products.name: compliance_permit
products.description: Master record for all regulatory operating permits held by the utility, including NPDES discharge permits, state drinking water permits, IUPs (Industrial User Permits), air quality permits, and stormwater permits. Tracks permit number, issuing authority (EPA, state primacy agency, NPDES), permit type, facility covered, effective and expiration dates, permitted limits, renewal status, and associated regulatory program (SDWA, CWA). Serves as the authoritative registry of all regulatory authorizations required to operate water and wastewater facilities.

attributes.name: analytical_method
attributes.description: The specific EPA-approved or Standard Methods analytical procedure required for measuring this parameter (e.g., 'EPA Method 1664A', 'Standard Methods 5210B', 'EPA Method 200.8', 'EPA Method 537.1 for PFAS', 'SM 2540D for TDS', 'SM 4500-H+ for pH').
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Methods for Chemical Analysis of Water and Wastes

attributes.name: compliance_evaluation_method
attributes.description: The method used to determine compliance with this condition: single value comparison (each result compared to limit), rolling average (moving average over specified period), statistical analysis (percentile or confidence interval), narrative assessment (qualitative evaluation), or best professional judgment (case-by-case determination).
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Compliance Inspection Manual

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this condition is subject to a compliance schedule (phased implementation plan) that allows the permittee additional time to achieve full compliance. True if a compliance schedule is in effect, False otherwise.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Writers Manual

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_milestone
attributes.description: Description of the compliance schedule milestone associated with this condition (e.g., 'Submit engineering plans by 2024-06-30', 'Complete construction by 2025-12-31', 'Achieve interim limit of 30 mg/L BOD by 2024-12-31'). Null if no compliance schedule applies.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Writers Manual

attributes.name: condition_number
attributes.description: The official condition number or identifier as stated in the permit document (e.g., 'I.A.1', 'II.B.3', 'Condition 5').
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Numbering Convention

attributes.name: condition_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the permit condition: active (currently enforceable), suspended (temporarily not enforced due to variance or stay), superseded (replaced by modified condition), expired (no longer in effect), or under appeal (contested by permittee).
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: condition_text
attributes.description: The full verbatim text of the permit condition as written in the permit document. Includes all narrative requirements, qualifications, and regulatory language.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Document

attributes.name: condition_type
attributes.description: Classification of the permit condition: effluent limit (numeric discharge limit), monitoring requirement (sampling frequency and method), reporting requirement (MOR/DMR submission), technology-based standard (treatment technology mandate), narrative condition (qualitative requirement), or best management practice (operational control).
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Writers Manual

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this permit condition record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: detection_limit_requirement
attributes.description: The minimum detection limit (MDL) or practical quantitation limit (PQL) required for the analytical method. Ensures that the laboratory can measure the parameter at levels sufficiently below the permit limit to demonstrate compliance. Null if no specific detection limit is mandated.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Methods for Chemical Analysis of Water and Wastes

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this permit condition becomes enforceable. May differ from the parent permit effective date if the condition has a phased implementation schedule.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: enforcement_priority
attributes.description: The priority level assigned by the regulatory agency for enforcement of this condition. Critical conditions (e.g., public health parameters like coliform, lead, PFAS) trigger immediate enforcement action upon violation. High priority conditions (e.g., BOD, TSS, pH) require prompt corrective action. Medium and low priority conditions may allow for compliance schedules.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Enforcement Management System (EMS)

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which this permit condition expires or is superseded. Typically aligns with the parent permit expiration date unless the condition is time-limited or subject to modification.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: The statistical basis for the effluent limit: daily maximum (highest single-day value), monthly average (arithmetic mean over calendar month), weekly average (arithmetic mean over 7-day period), instantaneous maximum (single grab sample), annual average, or minimum (for parameters like dissolved oxygen).
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Writers Manual

attributes.name: mixing_zone_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a mixing zone (limited area where discharge is allowed to exceed water quality standards before achieving full dilution and compliance) is authorized for this condition. True if mixing zone is allowed, False if end-of-pipe compliance is required.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Water Quality Standards Handbook

attributes.name: mixing_zone_description
attributes.description: Description of the authorized mixing zone including dimensions, boundaries, and compliance monitoring points (e.g., '100 meters downstream of Outfall 001', 'Within 50-foot radius of discharge point', 'Compliance measured at edge of mixing zone'). Null if no mixing zone is allowed.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Water Quality Standards Handbook

attributes.name: modification_date
attributes.description: The date on which this permit condition was last modified through permit amendment, administrative order, or consent decree. Null if the condition has never been modified since the original permit issuance.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: modification_reason
attributes.description: The reason for the most recent modification to this condition (e.g., 'Updated water quality standards', 'New analytical method approved', 'Compliance schedule adjustment', 'Facility upgrade completed', 'Enforcement action settlement', 'Anti-backsliding provision waiver'). Null if never modified.
attributes.references: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: The required frequency for monitoring or sampling this parameter: continuous (real-time SCADA monitoring), daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annually, or as needed (event-driven).
